The Gujarat Public Service Commission (GPSC) has officially released the List of Eligible Candidates for Application Scrutiny for two major recruitment advertisements - Advertisement No. 124/2025-26 for Deputy Executive Engineer (Civil), Class-2, and Advertisement No. 98/2025-26 for Inspector of Inspection of Building and Other Construction, Class-II. The result lists were published on 25 June 2026 and are available on the official GPSC portal. Candidates who appeared in the preliminary examination can now check whether their seat number appears in the eligible list and proceed with the online document upload process.

What Is the "List of Eligible Candidates for Application Scrutiny"?

Many candidates confuse this list with a final merit list - it is important to understand what this result actually means before taking any action.

This list is not a final merit list. It is a "Zone of Consideration" list - meaning it identifies only those candidates who are being called to submit their original documents for verification. Being on this list confirms that your preliminary exam score meets the minimum cutoff set by GPSC for your category. The final selection will be based on 50% weightage from the preliminary exam score and 50% weightage from the personal interview (Rubaru Mulakat).

GPSC Deputy Executive Engineer (Civil) Result 2026 - Advertisement No. 124/2025-26

This section covers all key details related to the GPSC Deputy Executive Engineer (Civil) Class-2 recruitment result published under Advertisement No. 124/2025-26.

Total Eligible Candidates

GPSC Inspector of Inspection Result 2026 - Advertisement No. 98/2025-26

This section provides full details on the eligible candidates list for the post of Inspector of Inspection of Building and Other Construction, Class-II, under the Labour, Skill Development and Employment Department.

Total Eligible Candidates

A total of 189 candidates have been declared eligible for application scrutiny for the post of Inspector of Inspection of Building and Other Construction, Class-II.

GPSC Preliminary Exam Details - How Was the Exam Conducted?

Understanding the exam structure helps candidates verify how their scores were calculated and why certain questions may have been cancelled.

The preliminary examination for both advertisements was conducted in two parts using the OMR method:

  • General Studies Paper: Held on 10 May 2026, jointly for 65 advertisements.
  • Subject-Specific Paper: Held on 03 May 2026, jointly for 10 advertisements.

For candidates who appeared in common/joint advertisements, a Self-Declaration was required - notified on 29 April 2026 (for General Studies) and 22 April 2026 (for Subject paper). Marks from the common advertisement have been credited accordingly.

GPSC Final Selection Process - Weightage for Exam and Interview

Eligible candidates must understand how the final merit list will be prepared, as the preliminary exam score is only one part of the selection process.

As per the GPSC office order dated 30 July 2016 (effective 01 August 2016), the final selection for direct recruitment will be based on:

  • 50% weightage from the marks obtained in the Preliminary Examination.
  • 50% weightage from the marks obtained in the Personal Interview (Rubaru Mulakat).

Documents Required for GPSC Application Scrutiny 2026

All eligible candidates must upload the required documents online at gpsc.gujarat.gov.in. Physical or postal submissions will not be accepted. Below is the complete list of documents required:

  1. Copy of SSC Credit Certificate (as proof of date of birth - school leaving certificate will not be accepted)
  2. Government Gazette copy or Marriage Registration Certificate (if name/surname has been changed)
  3. Caste Certificate from a competent authority (for SC, ST, and SEBC candidates)
  4. Appendix-K in Gujarati format with specific application number and date (for SEBC candidates) - Annexure-A in English or for central government recruitment will not be accepted
  5. Medical certificate in the prescribed format from a Government Hospital Superintendent/Civil Surgeon/Medical Board (for Divyang/PwD candidates)
  6. Copy of Discharge Book (for Ex-Servicemen candidates)
  7. Marriage Registration Certificate or gazette copy of name change (for married women candidates)
  8. Affidavit of non-remarriage (for widow candidates)
  9. Sports certificate in the prescribed format (if applicable, for Class-3 posts)
  10. All semester/year marksheets of graduation
  11. Graduation degree certificate
  12. All semester/year marksheets of post-graduation (if required as per advertisement)
  13. Post-graduation degree certificate (if required)
  14. Internship completion certificate (for medical, dental, and veterinary posts, if applicable)
  15. Council registration certificate (if required as per advertisement)
  16. PhD degree certificate (if required)
  17. NET/SLET certificate (if required)
  18. Proof of equivalence of foreign university degree (if applicable)
  19. Orders/authorization documents establishing the equivalence of qualification (if claiming equivalent qualification)
  20. No Objection Certificate in the prescribed format from the competent authority (for existing Gujarat Government employees - to be submitted in original at interview)
  21. Experience certificates (showing type of work, pay scale from start, and designation - as required per advertisement)
  22. Research papers (if required)
  23. Xerox copy of fee receipt (for unreserved/general category candidates)
  24. Medical certificate regarding physical measurements (if required)
  25. Any other relevant supporting documents as per the advertisement

Important: The complete list of applicable documents will be published on the GPSC official website under the respective advertisement number. Candidates must upload all documents online within the notified deadline. No documents will be accepted in person or by post.

How to Upload Documents for GPSC Application Scrutiny 2026

The document submission process is fully online. Here is a step-by-step guide for eligible candidates:

  1. Visit the official GPSC portal: gpsc.gujarat.gov.in
  2. Log in with your registered credentials.
  3. Navigate to Advertisement No. 124/2025-26 (DEE Civil) or 98/2025-26 (Inspector) as applicable.
  4. Open your confirmed online application form. If your photograph or signature is missing, attach a passport-size photo or sign the form again.
  5. Upload scanned copies of all required documents as listed in the official notification.
  6. Submit your application within the deadline notified by GPSC on their website.

Note: Applications submitted physically or by post will be automatically rejected. Only online submissions through the official portal are accepted.

What Happens After Application Scrutiny - Next Steps

Candidates who are found eligible after document verification will proceed to the personal interview stage. Here is what to expect:

  • After document scrutiny, GPSC will publish a separate list of candidates eligible for the Personal Interview (Rubaru Mulakat) on the official notice board and website.
  • If sufficient candidates are not found eligible for the interview from the current list, GPSC may provisionally add more candidates from the merit list who scored above the minimum qualifying marks (as per office orders dated 04 July 2025 and 17 September 2025).
  • Candidates with the same marks as the last eligible candidate in any category will also be considered eligible (tie-breaking rule applies).
  • Candidates who meet all eligibility requirements (education, age, experience) but are ranked below the required number after tie-breaking will not be called for the personal interview.
  • The final result after the interview will include all details of the seat numbers of candidates whose documents were verified.

What Is the GSSSB Wireman Provisional Result 2026?

This section explains what the provisional result actually means and why GSSSB has released it before the final selection list.

The GSSSB Wireman Provisional Result 2026 is a marks-disclosure document, not a final selection or merit list. It shows the marks scored by every candidate who appeared in the CBRT examination for Wireman, Class-3 (Advt No. 311/202526), based on the Final Answer Key. GSSSB has published this so candidates can verify their own scores before the board prepares the final merit list and proceeds with document verification.

GSSSB Wireman Result 2026 - Key Highlights

This section gives a quick snapshot of the most important details of the result for easy reference.

Particular Details
Organization Gujarat Subordinate Service Selection Board (GSSSB)
Post Name Wireman, Class-3
Advertisement No. 311/202526
Department Road and Buildings Department (Electrical Division)
Total Vacancies 66
Exam Mode MCQ-CBRT (Computer Based Recruitment Test)
Total Candidates Appeared 11,606
Result Declared On 25 June 2026
Result Type Provisional
Official Website gsssb.gujarat.gov.in

Background: From Answer Key to Final Result

This section traces the sequence of events that led up to the declaration of the provisional result, which helps candidates understand how their final marks were calculated.

GSSSB had earlier published a Provisional Answer Key for the Wireman CBRT exam and invited objections from candidates. After examining these objections with subject matter experts, the board released the Final Answer Key on 6 June 2026. The marks shown in the current provisional result have been calculated strictly on the basis of this Final Answer Key.

Exam Pattern and Marking Scheme

This section explains how the 210-question paper was structured and how marks were calculated for each section, which is essential for understanding the scores shown in the result PDF.

The Wireman CBRT exam consisted of two parts:

  • Part-A: Originally 60 questions worth 60 marks. One question was later cancelled based on the Final Answer Key, so marks for Part-A were calculated out of the remaining 59 questions. Each correct answer was awarded +1.01695 marks, and each incorrect answer attracted a penalty of -0.25424 marks.
  • Part-B: 150 questions worth 150 marks. Each correct answer was awarded +1.00 mark, and each incorrect answer attracted a penalty of -0.25 marks.

This means the maximum combined score remains 210 marks (60 in Part-A plus 150 in Part-B), even though the per-question value in Part-A was adjusted upward to compensate for the cancelled question.

How to Check GSSSB Wireman Provisional Result 2026

This section provides the exact steps candidates need to follow to find their marks in the official result PDF.

Candidates can check their result by following these steps:

  • Visit the official GSSSB website at gsssb.gujarat.gov.in.
  • Look for the notice titled "Wireman, Class-3 (Advt No. 311/2025-26) — Provisional Result."
  • Open the linked Annexure-A PDF document.
  • Use Ctrl+F (or the search function) to locate your Roll Number or Confirmation Number.
  • Note your Part-A marks, Part-B marks, and Total Marks shown against your name.

Details Available in the Result PDF

This section lists the specific data fields published for each candidate in the Annexure-A document.

For every candidate, the result PDF displays:

  • Confirmation Number
  • Roll Number
  • Full Name
  • Birth Date
  • Gender
  • Caste Category
  • Applicable reservation/relaxation column (Ex-Serviceman, Sports, Widow, PH Group, where applicable)
  • Marks obtained in Part-A
  • Marks obtained in Part-B
  • Total Marks

What Happens After the Provisional Result?

This section clarifies the next steps in the recruitment process, since the provisional result is not the end of the selection cycle.

Since this is a provisional result, it is not the final selection list. GSSSB will use these marks to prepare the final merit list for the 66 Wireman vacancies, after which shortlisted candidates will be called for document verification. Candidates are advised to keep checking the official GSSSB website for further notices regarding the merit list and verification schedule.

What Is a Merit-Wise Broadsheet in PSSSB?

This section explains what the merit-wise broadsheet means for candidates, so they can clearly understand their position in the PSSSB selection process.

A merit-wise broadsheet is the final selection document published by PSSSB that lists candidates in order of their merit — from highest marks to lowest — after all stages of the selection process are complete. It is not merely a list of qualified candidates; it is the document that determines the actual appointment order. For the Junior Technician and Storekeeper posts under Advt. No. 13/2025, the broadsheet contains candidates' roll numbers, names, marks obtained in Part A (Punjabi Qualifying) and Part B (Technical/General Knowledge), category details, and final selection status. Candidates whose names appear in the broadsheet are considered selected and will be called for document verification and appointment formalities.

How to Check PSSSB Junior Technician and Storekeeper Result 2026

This section provides a step-by-step guide to help candidates easily find and download their result PDF from the official PSSSB website. Following these steps will save time and help avoid confusion.

Candidates can check the PSSSB result 2026 online without any login or registration. The result is published in downloadable PDF format on the official website. Here is how to access it:

  • Step 1: Visit the official PSSSB website at sssb.punjab.gov.in.
  • Step 2: Click on the "Results" section available on the left-hand side of the homepage.
  • Step 3: Look for the links corresponding to "Junior Technician (Civil/Electrical)" or "Storekeeper (Advt. No. 13/2025)."
  • Step 4: Click on the relevant PDF link for your post.
  • Step 5: Once the PDF opens, press Ctrl+F and type your roll number or name to quickly locate your entry.
  • Step 6: Check your marks, category, and selection status carefully.
  • Step 7: Download and save the PDF, and take a printout for future reference.

What Details Are Mentioned in the PSSSB Result PDF?

This section outlines exactly what information candidates can find inside the PSSSB Junior Technician and Storekeeper merit-wise broadsheet PDF.

The broadsheet result PDF contains comprehensive details for each candidate. Understanding what is included will help candidates verify their entries accurately:

  • Candidate's roll number and full name
  • Marks obtained in Part A - Punjabi Qualifying Test
  • Marks obtained in Part B - Technical and General Knowledge paper
  • Category (General/SC/ST/OBC/EWS/Ex-Serviceman, etc.)
  • Final selection status (Selected / Waitlisted / Not Selected)
  • Post name and advertisement number

Note: If a candidate's Part B column shows "NA," it means they did not qualify in Part A (the Punjabi Qualifying paper) and were therefore not evaluated further. "Absent" indicates the candidate did not appear in the examination.

PSSSB Junior Technician and Storekeeper - Selection Process

This section explains the full selection process for the PSSSB Junior Technician and Storekeeper recruitment under Advt. No. 13/2025, helping candidates understand what stage they have reached and what comes next.

The selection process for these posts involves two major stages. The written examination, conducted on 14 March 2026, consisted of Part A (Punjabi Qualifying) and Part B (Technical/General Knowledge). Candidates who cleared both parts were ranked on the merit list. The publication of the merit-wise broadsheet marks the conclusion of the written examination stage.

RSPCB JSO & JEE Educational Qualification

Candidates must fulfil specific academic criteria depending on the post they applied for. This section outlines the minimum educational qualification required for each post under the RSPCB JSO JEE Recruitment 2025.

Junior Scientific Officer (JSO)

Candidates must hold a First Class M.Sc. or M.S. degree in Chemistry, Soil Science, Environmental Science, or Microbiology from a recognised Indian university. They must also possess a B.Sc. or B.S. degree in any Science discipline, or an equivalent foreign qualification recognised by the relevant authority.

Junior Environmental Engineer (JEE)

Candidates must hold an M.Tech. or M.E. degree in Environmental Engineering obtained after completing a B.Tech. or B.E. in Biotechnology, Chemical, Civil, Mining, Environmental, or Textile Engineering. Alternatively, candidates holding a First Class B.Tech. or B.E. degree in any of these branches from a recognised Indian university or an equivalent foreign qualification are also eligible.

How to Download Bihar Havildar Clerk Result 2026 PDF

Candidates can download the BPSSC Bihar Havildar Clerk result 2026 directly from the official website. The result has been published as a PDF containing the roll numbers of all 320 shortlisted candidates. No login or registration ID is required to access the result. Follow these steps to check your result:

Step-by-Step Process to Check Bihar Havildar Clerk Result 2026

  1. Visit the official BPSSC website at bpssc.bihar.gov.in
  2. On the homepage, navigate to the "Home Guard" tab or the Notices/Results section
  3. Look for the link titled "Result of Written Examination - Havildar Clerk (Advt. No. 01/2026)"
  4. Click the link the result PDF will open in a new tab
  5. Press Ctrl + F (Find) and type your roll number in the search bar
  6. If your roll number appears in the list, you are shortlisted for the Physical Efficiency Test (PET)
  7. Download and save the PDF for future reference
  8. Take a printout for use during PET document verification

Direct PDF Link: Bihar Havildar Clerk Result 2026 - Official PDF

Details Mentioned in Bihar Havildar Clerk Result 2026 PDF

The official BPSSC result PDF for Bihar Havildar Clerk 2026 contains specific details that candidates must check carefully. The result document is an eligibility list not a marks scorecard and contains the following information:

  • Recruitment advertisement number (01/2026)
  • Post name: Havildar Clerk (Adhinayak Lipik)
  • Roll numbers of all 320 shortlisted candidates eligible for PET
  • Category-wise and gender-wise selection breakup
  • Category-wise cutoff scores along with date of birth tiebreaker details
  • Total number of appeared and disqualified candidates during the written exam
  • Instructions for appearing in the Physical Efficiency Test (PET)
  • Documents required at the time of PET
  • Date of issue of result and official seal of BPSSC

What Happens After Bihar Havildar Clerk Result 2026? - Next Steps

Candidates whose roll numbers appear in the result PDF must now focus on the next stage of the BPSSC Bihar Havildar Clerk selection process. The result notification confirms that all 320 shortlisted candidates must compulsorily appear in the Physical Efficiency Test (PET). Failure to appear in the PET on the scheduled date will lead to disqualification; no request for postponement will be entertained under any circumstances.

Physical Efficiency Test (PET) - Key Details

The PET for Bihar Home Guard Havildar Clerk recruitment 2026 will include three physical events:

  • Running (Daud)
  • High Jump (Unchi Kood)
  • Shot Put (Gola Phek)

The final merit list for appointment to the post of Havildar Clerk will be prepared based on the total marks obtained across all three PET events, not based on the written examination score. The minimum physical standards specified in Advertisement No. 01/2026 are applicable and no relaxation in physical standards will be permitted.

PET Admit Card

The PET admit card/call letter will be available on the BPSSC official website under the "Home Guard" tab after the PET schedule is notified separately via newspapers and the official website. No admit card will be dispatched by post. Candidates must download their admit cards online from bpssc.bihar.gov.in.

Documents Required at PET Stage

Candidates must carry the following original documents along with one set of self-attested photocopies at the time of the PET:

  • Valid photo ID (Voter ID, Driving Licence, Aadhaar Card, etc.)
  • Educational qualification certificate (Intermediate / equivalent)
  • Date of birth proof (Matriculation/10th certificate)
  • Caste certificate issued by a competent authority (for SC, ST, EBC, BC categories)
  • Non-creamy layer certificate (for OBC/EBC candidates issued on father's basis for married/unmarried women)
  • Bihar domicile/residential certificate (for all reserved category candidates)
  • EWS income and asset certificate for financial year 2024-25 (if applicable, in prescribed format as per Bihar Govt. notification dated 26 Feb 2019)
  • Printout of online application form receipt
  • Printout of the result PDF (roll number confirmation)

DSSSB PGT Geography Exam & Selection Process

The selection for the PGT Geography post was conducted through a single-tier online written examination. Here is a brief outline of the process followed by DSSSB for this recruitment cycle.

  • Online written examination (Tier-I scheme) was conducted on 25 July 2025 and 02 August 2025.
  • Marks statements of 2107 candidates who appeared in the Tier-I exam were uploaded on the OARS module of the Board's website.
  • Based on merit, 99 candidates were provisionally shortlisted and asked to upload their e-dossiers from 24 March 2026 to 07 April 2026.
  • Post/Department allocation was done on a merit-cum-preference basis as per candidates' preferences submitted in the OARS module.
  • The final provisional nomination is based solely on marks secured in the Tier-I examination and claims made in online application forms.

What Happens After the DSSSB PGT Geography Result 2026?

Provisional nomination does not guarantee final appointment. Candidates included in the result notice must be aware of the following next steps in the DSSSB PGT Geography recruitment process.

  • Document Verification: The User Department (Directorate of Education, GNCTD / NDMC) will scrutinize and verify all documents uploaded in the e-dossier, including educational qualifications, age, caste certificates, and other essential documents.
  • Eligibility Check: The User Department will verify eligibility as per Recruitment Rules and other conditions of advertisement No. 07/23. The cutoff date for eligibility is 07 February 2024.
  • Caste Certificate Verification: OBC candidates must ensure their certificate meets the creamy layer exclusion criteria. SC/ST/EWS/PwD category certificates will also be verified by the issuing authority.
  • Offer of Appointment: The competent authority of the User Department shall issue the appointment letter only after full verification and satisfaction of eligibility conditions.
  • Post Allocation is Final: Once a post or department is allocated, no change will be entertained or allowed by the Board.

Important Notes for Provisionally Nominated Candidates

Candidates who find their roll number in the DSSSB PGT Geography Result 2026 must take note of the following critical points before proceeding further.

  • Inclusion in the result notice does not confer any right to the post. Final appointment is subject to the User Department's complete satisfaction.
  • DSSSB has not undertaken scrutiny of documents uploaded in e-dossiers at this stage. Verification will be done by the User Department.
  • The candidature is liable to be cancelled if any eligibility condition of the Recruitment Rules is not fulfilled or if false information is found in the application form or e-dossier.
  • The decision of the User Department regarding eligibility of candidates shall be final and binding.
  • The recruitment process for PGT Geography (Post Code 812/23) is hereby closed with the issuance of this result notice.
  • DSSSB reserves the right to rectify errors and omissions at any stage.

How to Check DSSSB PGT Geography Result 2026 Online

Why Only the 87% Main List Was Declared

MPPSC followed a specific government directive that determines how selection results are split between main and provisional lists. Understanding this helps candidates know why no separate provisional list was issued.

As per MP Government General Administration Department letter No. 07-46/2021/Aa.Pra./Ek dated 29.09.2022, the total vacancies are divided into an 87% Main List and a 13% Provisional List. However, since only 01 post was advertised for the OBC (Other Backward Class) category, the number of vacancies for the 13% provisional list becomes zero (nil). Minimum Qualifying Marks for MPPSC Internal Audit Officer Interview 2026

MPPSC prescribed category-wise minimum qualifying marks for the interview stage. Candidates who scored below these thresholds were treated as ineligible for selection.

  • Unreserved (General) Category: Minimum 41% marks in the interview (i.e., 41 out of 100)
  • SC, ST, OBC (Non-Creamy Layer), and Other Backward Classes (MP Domicile): Minimum 31% marks (i.e., 31 out of 100)
  • Economically Weaker Section (EWS): Minimum 31% marks

Candidates who scored below the applicable minimum qualifying marks were declared ineligible (Ayogy) and have not been considered in the final merit list.

Tie-Breaking Rules Applied in Selection

In cases where two or more candidates obtained equal interview marks, MPPSC applied a defined tie-breaking policy to decide merit rank. This ensures a fair and transparent selection process.

  1. Merit was first decided on the basis of the higher interview score itself.
  2. If interview scores were equal, the candidate with a higher percentage in the qualifying examination (as mentioned in the advertisement) was given priority.
  3. If the qualifying examination percentage was also equal, the older (senior in age) candidate was given preference.

  • Resignation: Some candidates join but resign shortly afterward, freeing up their position.

Rather than running an entirely new selection process, SBI fills these vacancies from the existing pool of candidates who appeared in the merit list but missed selection by a narrow margin.

Candidates whose roll numbers appear in the 1st Waiting List are only provisionally selected.   • Joining formalities and reporting date

Candidates called for document verification should keep the following ready:

If a candidate fails to produce the required documents or does not meet the eligibility criteria, the bank can cancel their provisional selection.

The Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Municipal Corporation (CSMC) has released the CSMC Hall Ticket 2026 on 25 June 2026 on the official IBPS portal. Candidates who applied for the CSMC Recruitment 2026 against 222 Group C vacancies can now download their admit card using their registration details. The CSMC written exam is scheduled for 9 July 2026, and the hall ticket carries essential details such as exam date, exam city, reporting time, and venue guidelines. This article covers the direct download link, step-by-step download process, exam date, vacancy details, and other important information related to CSMC Recruitment 2026.

CSMC Hall Ticket 2026 Download Link

Candidates need a direct, working link to access their admit card without confusion. The CSMC Hall Ticket 2026 has been activated on the IBPS registration portal and is available for download until the exam date.

The CSMC Hall Ticket 2026 was released on 25 June 2026 on the official IBPS website. Candidates appearing for the written exam on 9 July 2026 can download their admit card using the link below. The hall ticket must be downloaded before the last date, which is 9 July 2026, as it is mandatory to carry it to the exam hall.

Download CSMC Hall Ticket 2026 – Direct Link

How to Download CSMC Admit Card 2026?

Many first-time applicants are unsure how to access their hall ticket on the IBPS portal. The process is simple and only requires basic registration credentials.

Follow these steps to download the CSMC Hall Ticket 2026:

  1. Click on the official CSMC hall ticket link given above.
  2. Enter your registration number/roll number and date of birth or password.
  3. Submit the login details to proceed.
  4. The CSMC Admit Card 2026 will appear on the screen.
  5. Check all details printed on the hall ticket carefully.
  6. Download and save the admit card.
  7. Take a clear printout for the exam day.

CSMC Exam Date 2026

Candidates need to know the exact exam date and reporting guidelines to plan their exam day accordingly.

The CSMC Exam 2026 is scheduled to be held on 9 July 2026. All candidates who successfully applied for the CSMC Recruitment 2026 and have downloaded their hall ticket are eligible to appear. Candidates are advised to reach the exam centre at least one hour before the reporting time mentioned on the admit card.

Details Mentioned on CSMC Hall Ticket 2026

The hall ticket is not just an entry pass it contains several details candidates must verify before the exam.

The CSMC Admit Card 2026 includes the following details:

  • Candidate's name and roll number
  • Exam date and reporting time
  • Exam city and exam centre address
  • Candidate's photograph and signature
  • Post applied for
  • Exam day guidelines and instructions
  • Important do's and don'ts for the examination hall

Candidates should immediately report any discrepancy in personal details to the CSMC/IBPS helpdesk for correction before the exam date.

CSMC Recruitment 2026 Notification: Brief Overview

Understanding the background of the recruitment drive helps candidates connect the hall ticket to the larger selection process.

The CSMC Recruitment 2026 notification was released on 16 February 2026 for a total of 222 Group C vacancies across departments such as Engineering, Fire Service, Technical Service, Public Health, Veterinary, and Accounts/Audit. Major posts include Junior Engineer (Civil), Fireman, Sub Fire Station Officer, Driver-Operator, Sanitation Inspector, and Cashier, among others.

CSMC Selection Process 2026

Candidates downloading their hall ticket are appearing for the first stage of a multi-step selection process.

The CSMC selection process includes the following stages:

  • Merit List: Released after successful document verification

What to Carry on CSMC Exam Day?

Candidates often miss essential items on exam day, which can lead to entry being denied at the centre.

Candidates must carry the following to the CSMC exam centre on 9 July 2026:

What Is the APPSC Junior Assistant Hall Ticket?

This section explains what the hall ticket is and why it matters for exam-day entry.

The hall ticket (admit card) is an official document issued by APPSC that confirms a candidate's registration for the Junior Assistant cum Computer Operator written examination. It carries identity and exam-logistics details and acts as the primary entry pass at the test centre no candidate is permitted inside the exam hall without it.

How to Download the APPSC Junior Assistant Hall Ticket 2026

This section covers the exact step-by-step login process used on the official APPSC hall ticket portal.

  1. Go to the official hall ticket portal: portal-psc.ap.gov.in/Download_HallTickets/LOGINFORM_OTHERS (or the main site psc.ap.gov.in).
  2. Locate and click the link related to "Junior Assistant cum Computer Operator" hall ticket download under the Download Hall Tickets section.
  3. Enter your OTPR ID and Password, then complete the captcha.
  4. Select your applied post/notification if prompted, and click Submit.
  5. Your hall ticket will display on screen download it as a PDF and take a clear printout.

Information Printed on the Hall Ticket

  • Candidate name, photograph, and signature
  • Father's/Mother's name
  • Roll number and exam centre code

  • Aadhaar Card
  • PAN Card
  • Voter ID

  • Driving Licence
  • College/Employee ID (where applicable)

What If You Can't Download the Hall Ticket?

This section gives quick fixes for common login or access issues on the portal.

If the hall ticket doesn't load or login fails, try these steps before contacting support:

  • Clear your browser cache and cookies, or try a different browser/device

RBI Grade B Phase 1 Admit Card 2026 - Released

The Phase 1 exam is qualifying in nature only scores from this stage are used solely to shortlist candidates for Phase 2 (Mains). Marks from Phase 1 do not contribute to the final merit list.

RBI Grade B Mains Admit Card 2026 - Expected in July

With Phase 1 completed, all attention now turns to the RBI Grade B Phase 2 Mains Admit Card 2026, which is expected to be released in July 2026, ahead of the Mains exam scheduled on 25th July 2026 for General posts and 26th July 2026 for DEPR/DSIM posts. RBI typically releases the Mains hall ticket approximately 7 to 10 days before the exam date, so candidates should watch the official website closely during the second week of July.

The Mains exam is a comprehensive paper that tests a candidate's knowledge of Economic and Social Issues, Finance and Management, and English Writing Skills. Unlike Phase 1, Phase 2 marks are directly counted in the final selection.

Downloading the RBI Grade B call letter is a straightforward process. The same steps apply for both Phase 1 (already released) and Phase 2 (upcoming). Follow the steps below to access your hall ticket from the official website.

Understanding the exam pattern helps candidates prepare effectively for both phases of the selection process. The RBI Grade B selection consists of Phase 1 (Prelims), Phase 2 (Mains), and an Interview round.

Phase 1 Exam Pattern - Objective Type (Qualifying)

Phase 1 is a 2-hour online objective exam carrying 200 marks across 200 questions. Since it is only qualifying, candidates must clear it to advance to Mains, but these marks do not count toward the final score.

Paper II English (Writing Skills) Descriptive 100 90 Minutes

RBI has issued specific instructions that every candidate must follow on exam day. Non-compliance may result in disqualification from the examination.

Candidates must reach the exam centre before the gate closing time without fail. Biometric verification including thumb impression and photograph capture will be conducted at the centre. Ensure your name on the admit card matches exactly with your photo ID. Wearing clothes with metal items, large buttons, or accessories that could trigger security checks should be avoided. Electronic devices including mobile phones, smart watches, Bluetooth devices, calculators, and books are strictly prohibited inside the examination hall. The exam centre and date allotted on the call letter are final no requests for change of centre, date, or session will be entertained.

Eligibility Criteria for Teacher (Public Administration)

To be eligible for Post Code 26034, candidates must meet:

  • A Master's Degree in Public Administration from a recognized university with a minimum of 50% marks in aggregate
  • A Bachelor of Education (B.Ed.) with minimum 50% marks
  • A passed Teacher Eligibility Test (TET), conducted by the H.P. Board of School Education, Dharamshala, or another government-authorized agency

  • HP-domiciled SC/ST/OBC/PwBD candidates get a 5% relaxation in the minimum qualifying marks

Engagement Terms

Selected Public Administration Teachers will receive a fixed honorarium of ₹30,000 per month, paid for 10 months in an academic year, under a 5-year scheme-based engagement. This is a contractual position it does not count as regular government service, and benefits like pension, DA, HRA, or TA do not apply.

HPRCA Teacher Selection Process 2026

This section explains what happens after the CBT, so candidates know what to expect once the admit card stage is over.

The selection process for all HPRCA Teacher posts, including Public Administration, follows these stages:

  1. Computer Based Test (CBT) / OMR Screening Test 120 marks, objective MCQs, 90 minutes duration. No personal interview is conducted.
  2. Qualifying Marks Minimum 45% for General category and 40% for SC/ST/OBC/WFB categories (subject to relaxation if insufficient candidates qualify).
  3. Normalization If the CBT is held across multiple shifts, scores are normalized using the Z-Score (Mean and Standard Deviation) method.
  4. Merit List & Waiting Panel A category-wise merit list is prepared based on CBT marks; ties are resolved using marks in the essential qualification, then age (senior preferred), then alphabetically.
  5. Document Verification Shortlisted candidates must produce original certificates and self-attested photocopies for verification.

  • Double-check that you are using the correct Application ID and password used during registration
  • Clear your browser cache or try a different browser if the page doesn't load
  • Confirm that the admit card for your specific post and post code has actually been released HPRCA activates links post-wise, not all at once
  • If your roll number or details appear incorrect, contact HPRCA immediately through the official contact details on hprca.hp.gov.in rather than waiting until exam day

Common Issues & Solutions While Downloading City Slip

Issue #1: Unable to Login / Invalid Credentials Error

Solutions:

  • Verify your registration number carefully (no spaces before/after)
  • Check date of birth format if using DOB: DD/MM/YYYY
  • Ensure CAPS LOCK is off while entering details
  • Clear your browser cache and cookies (Ctrl+Shift+Del)
  • Try using a different web browser (Chrome, Firefox, or Edge)
  • Use “Forgot Password” link if needed
  • Check your registered email for confirmation details

Issue #2: City Slip Not Showing / Page Not Loading

Solutions:

  • Verify if city slip is released for your slot
  • Try downloading during non-peak hours (early morning or late night)
  • Disable VPN, proxy, or ad-blocker extensions
  • Check your internet connection stability
  • Try using mobile data instead of WiFi (or vice versa)
  • Use incognito/private browsing mode
  • Update your web browser to the latest version

Issue #3: Error in Details Displayed on City Slip

Solutions:

  • Contact SSC helpdesk immediately via regional offices
  • Email or call with screenshot and registration details
  • Keep your registration number ready
  • Explain the exact discrepancy in detail
  • Request for correction before exam date

Issue #4: PDF Download Not Working

Solutions:

  • Take a screenshot of the city slip as backup
  • Try “Print to PDF” option (Ctrl+P then save as PDF)
  • Use a different PDF reader (Adobe Acrobat Reader)
  • Check if pop-ups are blocked in browser settings
  • Ensure sufficient storage space on device
  • Try downloading from different device

Issue #5: Captcha Not Visible or Loading

Solutions:

  • Refresh the page (F5 key)
  • Enable JavaScript in browser settings
  • Disable browser extensions temporarily
  • Use a different browser
  • Clear browser cache completely

Use for Travel Booking Yes - Use for advance planning Can use after release

Download your city intimation slip as soon as it is released to avoid server overload and last-minute technical issues. The website may experience heavy traffic during peak hours.

Details Available in SSC City Intimation Slip 2026

When you download your city intimation slip, you will find the following information:

Information Type Details
Candidate Name Full name as per application form
Registration Number Unique registration ID
Exam Name Stenographer Grade C & D Skill Test
Exam City/State Name of city and state where skill test center is located
Skill Test Date 28, 29 January 2026
Important Instructions Dos and Don’ts for skill test day

Note: The exact skill test center address will be mentioned only in the admit card, which will be released 2-3 days before your scheduled date. The city slip only mentions the exam city name.

SSC Stenographer Recruitment 2025 (Skill Test 2026) - Important Dates

Event Date Status
Application Start Date 06 June 2025 Completed
Application End Date 26 June 2025 Completed
Exam Dates 06-08 August 2025 Completed
Result  28 November 2025 Completed
Skill Test City Intimation Slip Release 21 January 2026 Live Now
Skill Test Admit Card 2-3 days before skill test Upcoming
Skill Test Dates 28, 29 January 2026 Upcoming
Final Result Declaration To be announced Not yet

Common Issues & Solutions While Downloading City Slip

Issue #1: Unable to Login / Invalid Credentials Error

Solutions:

  • Verify your registration number carefully (no spaces)
  • Ensure correct password (case-sensitive)
  • Clear browser cache and cookies
  • Try different browser
  • Use "Forgot Password" if needed

Issue #2: City Slip Not Showing / Page Not Loading

Solutions:

  • Check during non-peak hours
  • Disable VPN/ad-blockers
  • Use incognito mode
  • Try mobile data

Issue #3: Error in Details Displayed on City Slip

Solutions:

  • Contact SSC helpdesk immediately with screenshot
  • Explain discrepancy with registration details

City Intimation Slip vs Admit Card - Key Differences

Many candidates confuse city intimation slip with admit card. Here’s a clear comparison:

Aspect City Intimation Slip Admit Card
Purpose Advance information for travel planning Mandatory entry document
Release Time Before admit card 2-3 days before skill test
Information Provided Exam city only Full center address, instructions
Can you appear in test? NO YES (Mandatory)
Exam Center Address Only city name Complete details

Critical Warning: You CANNOT appear for the skill test with only the city intimation slip. You MUST download and carry the admit card along with valid ID proof.

The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) has released Advertisement No. 07/2026 on 25 June 2026, inviting online recruitment applications for 54 posts spread across multiple central government ministries and departments. The vacancies include positions such as Drug Inspector (186 posts), Specialist Grade III Assistant Professor across various medical specialities, Aeronautical Officer (11), Legal Officer (12), Company Prosecutor (18), and several others. Eligible candidates can apply online from 25 June 2026 up to 17 July 2026 at 6:00 PM through UPSC's official portal at upsconline.nic.in. The application fee is ₹25 for General/OBC/EWS male candidates; women, SC, ST, and PwBD candidates are fully exempted.

UPSC Advertisement 07/2026 – Eligibility Criteria, Age Limit & Qualifications

Eligibility requirements for UPSC Advt No. 07/2026 vary significantly by post, as these are specialist and technical positions spanning engineering, law, medicine, and administration. All candidates must be Indian citizens. The closing date for submission of the online application - 17 July 2026 - is the reference date for determining eligibility in every respect.

Selected Post-Wise Essential Qualifications

Post Essential Qualification (Educational) Experience Required
Joint Director (Crops Development Directorate) Master's Degree in Agricultural Economics / Agricultural Extension / Agronomy / Entomology / Nematology / Genetics & Plant Breeding / Agriculture Botany / Plant Bio Technology / Plant Pathology / Plant Physiology / Seeds Science & Technology / Soil Science & Agricultural Chemistry from a recognised university OR Bachelor's Degree in Agricultural Engineering 3 years in production/productivity/planning/development/extension in food or cash crops in a govt. / semi-govt. / PSU / autonomous body / recognised research institute / agricultural university

Age Limit – Post-Wise (Key Posts)

Age limits differ by post and category. Candidates wondering about age relaxation can note that PwBD candidates receive an additional 10 years of relaxation over and above the prescribed upper age limit, and the maximum age for PwBD candidates shall not exceed 56 years in any case. Ex-Servicemen and Central Government servants are also entitled to age relaxation as per central government rules.

General Age Relaxation Rules

  • OBC candidates: 3 years relaxation over UR upper age limit.
  • SC/ST candidates: 5 years relaxation over UR upper age limit.
  • PwBD (UR): 10 years; PwBD (OBC): 13 years; PwBD (SC/ST): 15 years. Maximum age cap: 56 years.
  • Ex-Servicemen: 5 years relaxation, subject to the condition that continuous service rendered is not less than 6 months after attestation as on the closing date.
  • Central/UT Government Servants: Up to 5 years, subject to 3 years continuous regular service in the same line or allied cadre.

UPSC Advt No. 07/2026 Application Fee

The application fee for UPSC Advertisement 07/2026 is nominal at ₹25 (Rupees Twenty-Five only) for General, OBC, and EWS male candidates. Female candidates of all categories, as well as SC, ST, and Persons with Benchmark Disability (PwBD) candidates, are fully exempted from payment of fee. The fee can be paid online using Visa, Master, or RuPay credit/debit cards, UPI, or internet banking of any bank.

Female Candidates (All Categories) Nil (Exempted)
SC / ST (Male) Nil (Exempted)
Persons with Benchmark Disability – PwBD (All) Nil (Exempted)

Important: Applications submitted without the prescribed fee will be summarily rejected. Fee once paid is non-refundable and cannot be held in reserve for any other examination or selection.

UPSC Recruitment 2026 (Advt 07) – Selection Process

The selection process for UPSC Advertisement No. 07/2026 varies by post. For most posts, it consists of shortlisting based on the online application, followed by a Recruitment Test (RT) or Combined Recruitment Test (CRT) if warranted, and then a Personality Test (Interview). Candidates will be shortlisted for interview based on the information provided in their online application and their performance in the RT, if held.

  1. Online Application Submission: Submit application at upsconline.nic.in by 17 July 2026.
  2. Shortlisting: UPSC shortlists candidates on the basis of information provided in the online application. Incorrect information may lead to rejection through computer-based shortlisting.
  3. Recruitment Test (RT) / Combined Recruitment Test (CRT) – if applicable: For posts where the number of applications is large, UPSC may conduct an RT or CRT before the interview. The test is ordinarily conducted at the following centres: Ahmedabad, Bhopal, Chennai, Delhi, Dispur (Guwahati), Jaipur, Jammu, Kochi, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, Nagpur, Port Blair, Ranchi, and Visakhapatnam.
  4. Personality Test / Interview: Shortlisted candidates are called for interview. Candidates must bring the printout of their online application and all original/self-attested copies of supporting documents.
  5. Final Selection and Appointment: Appointment orders are issued by the respective Ministry/Department. UPSC may grant higher initial pay to candidates adjudged meritorious at the interview stage.

UPSC Advt 07/2026 – Salary & Pay Scale (7th CPC Pay Matrix)

Selected candidates will receive pay as per the 7th Central Pay Commission Pay Matrix. The pay level ranges from Level-7 for posts such as Company Prosecutor and Photographic Officer to Level-11 (with NPA) for medical Specialist Grade III posts. In addition to basic pay, candidates are entitled to Dearness Allowance, HRA, and other admissible allowances as per Central Government rules.

UPSC Advertisement 07/2026 Apply Online – Step-by-Step Guide

The UPSC online recruitment application for Advt No. 07/2026 must be submitted through the official UPSC ORA (Online Recruitment Application) portal at upsconline.nic.in. The last date to apply online is 17 July 2026 at 6:00 PM (1800 Hrs). Candidates are advised to submit their application well in advance to avoid last-minute technical difficulties.

  1. Visit the UPSC ORA portal: upsconline.nic.in/ora/
  2. Register and create your profile if you have not already done so. Have your Aadhaar Card / Voter ID / PAN Card / Passport / Driving Licence or any other government-issued photo ID ready for Universal Registration (URN) profile creation.
  3. Log in with your credentials.
  4. Select Advertisement No. 07/2026 and choose the specific post/vacancy number you wish to apply for.
  5. Fill in all personal, educational, and professional details accurately. Ensure all information is correct - wrong information may lead to computer-based rejection and debarment by the Commission.
  6. Upload required documents/certificates applicable to your category - caste, disability, ex-serviceman, orphan, sports, project-affected, earthquake-affected certificates as applicable.
  7. Pay the application fee of ₹25 online via Visa/Master/RuPay credit or debit card, UPI, or internet banking (fee exempted for Female/SC/ST/PwBD candidates).
  8. Review all details carefully and submit the application form. Note: Candidates will NOT be allowed to withdraw their application after submission.
  9. Take a printout of the finally submitted Online Recruitment Application for future reference.
  10. Enter your correct and active e-mail address in the application - all correspondence from UPSC, including interview schedules, will be sent to this e-mail ID only.

UPSC Advertisement 07/2026 Apply Online Here

Documents Required for UPSC Advt 07/2026 – Interview Stage

Candidates are not required to send any documents to UPSC at the time of application submission. However, all shortlisted candidates called for the interview must carry original documents and self-attested photocopies. Failure to produce required documents at the interview stage will result in disqualification and forfeiture of travelling allowance reimbursement.

  • Printout of the submitted Online Recruitment Application
  • Photo ID proof (Aadhaar / Voter Card / PAN / Passport / Driving Licence)
  • Date of birth certificate (Matriculation / SSC certificate)
  • Educational qualification certificates (degree, diploma, mark sheets)
  • Experience certificates from all previous/current employers
  • Caste/Category certificate (SC/ST/OBC/EWS) in prescribed proforma from competent authority
  • PwBD disability certificate (minimum 40% disability) in prescribed proforma
  • Certificate for professional registration (where applicable, e.g. NMC/MCI registration for medical posts)
  • Language/publication/NET/GATE/conference/internship certificates if claimed
  • Age relaxation certificate for Ex-Servicemen / Central Government employees in prescribed proforma issued after the date of advertisement
  • Declaration of intimation to Head of Office/Department (for persons already in regular Government service)
  • Documents in language other than Hindi/English must be accompanied by a transcript duly attested by a Gazetted Officer or Notary.

Common Mistakes to Avoid – UPSC Advt 07/2026 Application

Given the large number of posts and the diverse eligibility conditions in UPSC Advertisement No. 07/2026, there are several common errors candidates make. Correcting these proactively can prevent outright rejection before the interview stage.

  • Applying for a post you do not meet the exact qualification for: UPSC shortlists strictly on the basis of declared qualifications. Applying with a "similar" or "equivalent" degree without a formal equivalence order from the competent authority is grounds for rejection. Produce the equivalence order if claiming an equivalent qualification.
  • Entering an inactive or incorrect e-mail address: UPSC sends all interview schedules and document requirements exclusively by e-mail. A wrong email means you will miss the interview call entirely. Double-check before submitting.
  • Submitting incomplete category documents later: All category-based claims (caste, disability, ex-serviceman) must be supportable at the interview stage with original documents in the prescribed UPSC proforma - not general certificates from hospitals or district offices.
  • Not declaring government service: Persons already in regular government service must submit a declaration to UPSC that they have informed their Head of Office in writing. Omitting this can lead to disciplinary consequences.
  • Attempting to withdraw the application after submission: UPSC explicitly states that candidates will not be allowed to withdraw their application once submitted. Apply only if you are genuinely eligible and intend to participate.
  • Bringing a mobile phone to the exam/interview venue: Mobile phones and all electronic devices are strictly banned at UPSC examination/interview halls - even in switched-off mode. Violation results in debarment from future examinations.
  • Waiting until the last day: The portal closes at exactly 1800 Hrs on 17 July 2026. Server congestion near the deadline is common. Complete your application at least 2–3 days in advance.
  • Submitting documents in a language other than Hindi/English without a notarised transcript: Any certificate in a regional language must be accompanied by a transcript attested by a Gazetted Officer or Notary.

Who Can Apply? - NIACL Apprentice 2026 Eligibility Criteria

Understanding the eligibility criteria is the first and most critical step before applying. Here is a detailed breakdown of all conditions you must satisfy.

Nationality

All applicants must be citizens of India.

Educational Qualification

Candidates must hold a graduate degree in any discipline from a recognized university, or an equivalent qualification recognized by the Central Government.

Crucially, the final year mark sheet date must fall between January 1, 2022 and June 1, 2026 (both dates inclusive). Graduates who passed before January 1, 2022, or after June 1, 2026, are not eligible.

Prior Apprenticeship Condition

  • Candidates must not have previously undergone apprenticeship training under the Apprentices Act 1961 - either with NIACL or any other organization.
  • Candidates currently pursuing an apprenticeship anywhere are also ineligible.
  • Candidates with one or more years of job experience after graduation are not eligible.

Online Applications Are Now Open (June 23 – July 6, 2026)

The application process is a two-step procedure. Both steps must be completed for your application to be valid.

Important: Your application is only considered complete after the examination fee is successfully paid online. Incomplete applications will be automatically rejected.

Step-by-Step Application Process for NIACL Apprentice 2026

Here is a clear walkthrough of exactly what you need to do to successfully submit your application.

Documents to Keep Ready Before You Begin

Gather these before starting the registration to avoid interruptions:

  • Aadhaar Card
  • Valid personal email ID (for account activation and login)
  • Active mobile number
  • Passport-size photograph (JPEG format, under 1 MB)
  • Qualifying degree or provisional certificate (PDF format, under 1 MB)

Step-by-Step Process

1. Register on NATS Portal Visit https://nats.education.gov.in, create your account, and ensure your profile is 100% complete. Then apply specifically for The New India Assurance Company Limited's apprenticeship listing.

2. Note Your NATS Enrolment Number After applying on NATS, you will receive a unique NATS enrolment number. This is mandatory for the next step.

3. Apply on BFSI SSC Portal Go to https://beep.bfsissc.com/candidate_login. Fill in personal details, upload documents, enter your NATS enrolment number, choose your preferred state, and pay the examination fee.

4. Select Only One State Candidates can apply for only one state. Your training, if selected, will be at a Regional Office within that state based on the company's requirements.

5. Confirm Payment & Save Application After successful payment, take a printout of your completed online application form. No changes are permitted after final submission.

Selection Process - How NIACL Apprentices Are Chosen

Selection happens in two main stages after fee payment. Here is what to expect at each stage.

Stage 1 - Online Written Test (Objective Type)

The online exam is held from home (proctored), using your own camera-enabled device - desktop, laptop, tablet, or smartphone.

Total 100 100 -
  • Duration: 60 minutes
  • Tie-breaking rule: If two candidates score equally, the older candidate is ranked higher (descending age order).

Stage 2 - Regional Language Test & Document Verification

Candidates who clear the online written test are shortlisted in 3× the number of available seats per state per category for this stage.

  • Candidates who studied the regional language of their chosen state in Class 10 or 12 are exempt from the language test.
  • All others must demonstrate proficiency (reading, writing, speaking, and understanding) in the specified local language of the state.
  • Candidates failing the language test cannot be engaged as apprentices.

Document Verification Checklist

Carry originals plus self-attested photocopies of:

  1. Photo ID proof (Aadhaar / PAN / Voter ID / Driving License / Passport)
  2. Class 10 certificate (as proof of date of birth)
  3. Class 12 marksheets and graduation marksheets (semester/year-wise) with degree
  4. CGPA-to-percentage conversion certificate (if applicable)
  5. SC / ST / OBC / EWS / PwBD certificates with required declarations

Stipend, Training Conditions & What to Expect

This section covers what apprentices receive during training and the rules governing their engagement.

Stipend & Payment

  • Monthly stipend: ₹12,300
  • Payment is made by the 10th day of the following month
  • No additional benefits, allowances, or statutory contributions (PF, Mediclaim, etc.) are provided
  • Pro-rata deduction applies for unauthorized absences

Leave Policy

  • 1 day of leave per month, credited at the beginning of the next month
  • Leave can be carried forward but not more than 2 days at a time
  • All accumulated leave lapses at the end of the contract
  • Apprentices are entitled to all company-observed public holidays

Training Duration & Certification

  • Training period: 12 months
  • On completion, apprentices undergo an assessment (theory by BFSI SSC + practical by NIACL)
  • Successful candidates receive an Apprenticeship Certificate from BFSI SSC

Employment Disclaimer

It is important to note clearly: this is not a job offer. NIACL is under no obligation to offer employment after training, and apprentices have no right to claim a job. This is a training engagement, not a contract or regular employment.

Special Guidelines for Reserved Category Candidates

Certain candidate groups have specific rules they must be aware of before applying.

OBC Candidates

  • Only Non-Creamy Layer OBC candidates are entitled to OBC reservation benefits.
  • Creamy layer OBC candidates must apply under the General (Unreserved) category and meet General category age criteria.

EWS Candidates

  • Gross annual family income must be below ₹8 lakh, and the family must not own 5+ acres of agricultural land, 1000+ sq. ft. residential flat, or qualifying residential plots.

PwBD Candidates (Persons with Benchmark Disabilities)

  • Minimum disability of 40% is required for reservation benefits.
  • Eligible disability types: Visual Impairment (VI), Hearing Impairment (HI), Locomotor/Orthopedic (OH), Intellectual/Autism (ID), Multiple Disabilities (MD).
  • PwBD candidates using a scribe get 20 minutes of compensatory time per hour.
  • The scribe must not be a co-applicant for the same exam and cannot serve as scribe for more than one candidate.

About CRE-5: What Is It and Who Is It For?

CRE-5 is a unified, single-window recruitment platform that allows eligible candidates to apply once and be considered for similar posts across multiple participating institutes. The Examination Section, AIIMS New Delhi acts solely as the examination-conducting body; recruitment rules, service conditions, and final appointment decisions rest entirely with each participating institute independently.

Participating organizations are autonomous bodies or subordinate offices under the Government of India, functioning independently from AIIMS New Delhi. Candidates are advised to check each institute's individual recruitment rules and eligibility criteria before applying, as conditions may differ for the same post name across different institutes.

However, application fees paid by SC/ST candidates who appear in the examination will be refunded to the source account after declaration of results.

AIIMS CRE-5 Recruitment 2026 - Exam Pattern and Syllabus

The CRE-5 Computer Based Test is a structured, time-bound examination designed to assess both domain knowledge and general aptitude.

CBT Structure

Parameter Detail
Duration 90 minutes
Total Questions 100 MCQs
Total Marks 400 marks (4 marks per question)
Negative Marking -1 mark per wrong answer (1/4th deduction)
General Knowledge & Aptitude / Computer 20 MCQs
Domain-Specific Questions 80 MCQs
Sections 5 sections × 20 questions × 18 minutes each

Each section is sequential and time-locked - once a section closes, candidates cannot return to it. Candidates must attempt all possible questions within the active section's time window.

Medium of Examination

Posts where the essential qualification is 10th/12th will be examined in bilingual (English and Hindi) medium. Posts requiring bachelor's or higher qualifications, or posts involving specific technical domain knowledge, will be examined in English only.

Qualifying Marks

Category Qualifying Percentage
UR / EWS 40%
OBC 35%
SC / ST 30%
PwBD (all categories) 30%
Ex-Servicemen As per their category

Tie-Breaking Rules

In case of equal marks, ties are resolved in this order: (i) higher marks in the domain-specific section; (ii) fewer wrong answers/negative marks; (iii) older date of birth; (iv) alphabetical order of name, then father's name, then mother's name.

Skill Test

For selected post groups, a Skill Test is conducted as Stage II for candidates who qualify the CBT. The skill test is qualifying in nature. The final merit list is prepared based on CBT performance, but only among those who pass the skill test for the relevant post.

Posts requiring skill tests include groups such as Junior Administrative Assistant (typing test), Stenographer (stenography test), Programmer (computer skill test), Hindi Translator (translation test), Assistant Security Officer (PST), and Fire Technician (PET & PST). See Annexure-V of the DRA for complete scheme details.

If a candidate qualifies the CBT but fails the skill test, they remain eligible only for posts within the same group that do not require a skill test.

AIIMS CRE-5 Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

CRE-5 follows a multi-stage recruitment process. Each stage is mandatory for progression to the next.

Stage 1 - Online Application: Candidates register on www.aiimsexams.ac.in and submit applications by 03 July 2026.

Stage 2 - Application Acceptance: Application status published on 9 July 2026.

Stage 3 - Computer Based Test (CBT): Tentatively 25-27 July 2026 at examination centres across major states/UTs of India.

Stage 4 - Skill Test (where applicable): Conducted after CBT for qualifying candidates in applicable groups. Venue: preferably Delhi/NCR. Date to be notified.

Stage 5 - Choice & Preference: Qualified candidates are invited to exercise institute choices and indicate order of preference. Candidates who fail to exercise choices within the given period will not be considered for any institute.

Stage 6 - Seat Allocation: Allocation is made in order of merit based on choices exercised and eligibility at each participating institute.

Stage 7 - Document Verification: Original certificates verified by the respective AIIMS/Institute on the date notified by them.

Stage 8 - Joining: Selected candidates must report on the date specified in the result/allocation notice. Failure to report will lead to mandatory cancellation of candidature for CRE.

AIIMS CRE-5 Recruitment 2026 - How to Apply for AIIMS CRE-5 2026

Applications can only be submitted through the Online Registration Terminal (OTR) at www.aiimsexams.ac.in. Physical documents must not be sent; no correspondence regarding correction in registration will be entertained.

  1. Visit the official website: www.aiimsexams.ac.in
  2. Register through the OTR (One-Time Registration) portal if you have not already done so.
  3. Log in and select the CRE-5 application link.
  4. Fill in all details carefully - name, date of birth, category, qualification, experience, and NOC details if applicable.
  5. Upload photographs, signature, and left thumb impression in the format specified under "Upload Image Instructions."
  6. Select your examination centre preference (state/UT).
  7. Pay the applicable examination fee via Debit Card, Credit Card, or Net Banking.
  8. Submit the application and download the registration slip for your records.
  9. If you are working in a Government/PSU/Autonomous Body, upload the No Objection Certificate (NOC) from your current employer by 6 July 2026 - failing to do so will prevent you from appearing in the examination.
  10. Check your application status on 9 July 2026 at www.aiimsexams.ac.in.

Eligibility Criteria – 130 INF BN TA ECO KUMAON Recruitment Rally 2026

Eligibility for the 130 INF BN TA ECO KUMAON Recruitment Rally 2026 is restricted to two specific candidate groups: ex-servicemen of the Armed Forces, and ex-women employees (including premature retirees) of the Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change (MoEF & CC) and the State Forest Department. Both groups must meet the service, medical, and character conditions listed below.

  • Enrolment window: Candidates should be enrolled within 5 years from their date of retirement.
  • Medical Category: SHAPE-I is required.
  • Character: Must be Exemplary or Very Good.
  • Qualification: Ex-servicemen must be of Indian Domicile and pension holders only. Ex-women employees (including premature retirees) of MoEF & CC and the State Forest Department must have rendered a minimum of 20 years of service in MoEF & CC or the State Forest Department.
  • Conduct: Candidates should not be involved in any civil or police cases.

Candidates wondering about the recruitment procedure can note that it differs by category. Ex-servicemen Male candidates undergo a physical fitness test - a 1.6 km run, pull-ups, a 9 ft ditch, and balance, all assessed as per age criteria - followed by a medical test and interview for those shortlisted. Ex-women employees of MoEF & CC and SFD instead go through an interview by the Board of Officers (BOO), a proficiency test in afforestation-related activity and nursery management conducted by the BOO, and a medical examination.

Salary & Engagement Terms – 130 INF BN TA ECO KUMAON Recruitment Rally 2026

SSC SSA Eligibility Criteria 2026 - Who Can Apply

The SSC SSA / UDC Limited Departmental Competitive Examination 2025 is open only to regularly appointed Lower Division Clerks (JSA/LDC) serving in the Central Secretariat Clerical Service (CSCS) cadre of DoPT. The crucial date for counting approved service is 1 August 2025. Candidates must satisfy all the following conditions before applying.

Length of Service Requirement

A candidate must have rendered not less than five years' approved and continuous service in the Lower Division Clerk Grade as on 01 August 2025. However, if the candidate was appointed to the LDC grade through a competitive examination (including a Limited Departmental Competitive Examination), the results of such examination must have been declared at least five years before the crucial date and the candidate must have rendered at least four years of approved and continuous service in that grade.

Typewriting Test Condition

Unless exempted, the candidate must have passed the typewriting test held by UPSC or SSC for confirmation in the Lower Division Clerk grade on or before the date of this notification. Candidates who have been granted exemption from the typewriting test must quote the order number and date of such exemption in the application form.

Deputation and Transfer Provisions

LDCs on deputation to ex-cadre posts with the approval of the competent authority are eligible to apply if they otherwise fulfill all eligibility criteria. However, a candidate who has been appointed to an ex-cadre post or another service on transfer without retaining a lien in the LDC grade is not eligible. A candidate who resigns, quits service, or whose services are terminated after applying will not be eligible for appointment on the result of this examination.

SSC SSA Exam Pattern 2026 - Scheme of Examination

The SSC Senior Secretariat Assistant exam 2026 is conducted in two parts. Part-I is a Computer Based Examination (CBE) of 200 marks with four subjects, each carrying 50 marks and 50 questions. Part-II is an evaluation of service records (APARs) worth 100 marks. The final rank of the candidate is determined by adding both Part-I and Part-II scores.

Part-I: Computer Based Examination (200 Marks)

Subject No. of Questions Maximum Marks Duration
Comprehension and General English 50 50 3 hours (4 hours for eligible scribe candidates)
Parliamentary Procedure 50 50
General Knowledge 50 50
Noting and Drafting 50 50
Total 200 200  

All questions are of Objective Type Multiple Choice format. There is a negative marking of 0.25 marks for each wrong answer. Candidates must attempt the examination in the language (English or Hindi) opted in the application form, except the "General English" section of the first subject, which must be attempted in English only. No Braille question paper will be provided.

Syllabus for Part-I CBE

Subject Syllabus
Comprehension and General English Simple composition and Applied Grammar
Parliamentary Procedure Simple questions on Parliament sessions and handling of Parliament questions
General Knowledge Current events, everyday observation and general information about India
Noting and Drafting Questions from Chapters 7, 8, and 9 of the latest CSMOP - Guidelines on Noting, Communication, Forms, Channels, Procedure, and Drafting of Communications

Part-II: Evaluation of Record of Service (100 Marks)

One hundred marks are earmarked for evaluation of Annual Performance Appraisal Reports (APARs). Only candidates who qualify Part-I (CBE) will be called for APAR evaluation. Marks from Part-II are added to the Part-I score to determine final merit. Once APARs are evaluated, no request for change in grading will be entertained.

SSC SSA UDC Selection Process 2026

The SSC SSA / UDC selection process 2026 is a two-stage merit-based system. Candidates must first clear the Computer Based Examination and are then shortlisted for APAR evaluation. The final rank is based on the combined aggregate of both stages. This is a competitive examination - success does not confer any right to selection unless the cadre authority is also satisfied about the candidate's suitability.

  1. Stage 1 - Computer Based Examination (Part-I): 200 marks across 4 objective-type subjects. The Commission may fix minimum qualifying marks at its discretion.
  2. Stage 2 - Evaluation of Service Records (Part-II): 100 marks based on APAR evaluation. Only Part-I qualifiers are considered.
  3. Final Merit: Aggregate of Part-I (200 marks) + Part-II (100 marks) = 300 marks total. Names of selected candidates will be arranged in order of merit for inclusion in the Select List of SSA/UDC of CSCS cadre.

Tie-Breaking Rules

When two or more candidates secure equal aggregate marks, ties are resolved in this order: (i) Marks in CBE overall, (ii) Marks in Comprehension and General English, (iii) Marks in Parliamentary Procedure, (iv) Marks in General Knowledge, (v) Date of birth - older candidate ranked higher, (vi) Alphabetical order of names.

Pay Scale - SSC SSA UDC Salary 2026

Candidates selected through the SSC Senior Secretariat Assistant Recruitment 2026 will be placed in the Pay Level-4 of the 7th Pay Commission Pay Matrix. The pay range for this Group C Non-Gazetted post is Rs. 25,500 to Rs. 81,100 per month. In addition to basic pay, all applicable central government allowances such as DA, HRA, and TA are admissible as per government rules.

Common Mistakes to Avoid - SSC SSA UDC Apply Online 2026

Based on the structure and requirements of this departmental exam, candidates must avoid the following errors that commonly lead to rejection or disqualification from the SSC Upper Division Clerk Limited Departmental Exam 2026.

  • Skipping the typewriting test details: The application requires specific information about whether the typewriting test was passed or exempted, including roll number and date. Leaving this blank or providing incorrect details is a common reason for application rejection.
  • Not creating a new OTR on ssc.gov.in: The OTR created on the old website (ssc.nic.in) is not valid on the new SSC website. Trying to log in with old credentials will fail - create a fresh OTR on ssc.gov.in.
  • Missing the departmental forwarding deadline: Submitting the online application on time is not enough. The printed copy must reach SSC (NR), New Delhi by 23 July 2026 through the HoD/HoO. Many candidates miss this step assuming online submission is sufficient.
  • Uploading a pre-existing photograph: The portal only accepts live photographs captured at the time of application. Uploading a pre-taken photo leads to summary rejection of the application.
  • Miniature or blurred signatures: The signature must be clearly visible and occupy at least 80% of the allocated box. Miniature, faded, or rotated signatures are the leading reasons for application rejection.
  • Applying without verifying service eligibility: Candidates must confirm that they have rendered at least five years of approved and continuous service in the LDC/JSA grade as on 01 August 2025 before applying.
  • Name/date of birth mismatch: Details in the application - name, father's name, date of birth - must exactly match the Matriculation certificate. Any discrepancy can cancel candidature.
  • Carrying electronic devices to the exam: Possession of mobile phones, Bluetooth devices, or any electronic gadget in the examination hall attracts a debarment of 3-5 years from all SSC examinations.
  • Changing appearance before the exam: Candidates must ensure their appearance on exam day closely matches the photograph in the application form. Examination staff can deny entry if there is a visible mismatch.

Eligibility Criteria – Who Can Apply for SSC JSA LDC DoPT LDCE 2025

This is a Limited Departmental Competitive Examination — it is NOT open to the general public. Only serving central government employees who meet specific service and educational conditions are eligible. The crucial date for determining eligibility is 1 August 2025. Candidates who have resigned, quit service, or whose services have been terminated after applying will not be eligible for appointment on the result of this examination.

Service Eligibility Conditions

  • Must be a permanent or regularly appointed temporary Group 'C' employee with Grade Pay of Rs. 1800.
  • Must have rendered not less than 3 years of regular service as a Group 'C' employee with Grade Pay of Rs. 1800 as on the crucial date of 1 August 2025.
  • A Group 'C' employee on deputation to an ex-cadre post with approval of competent authority is also eligible, if otherwise eligible.
  • A Group 'C' employee appointed to an ex-cadre post or another service on transfer who continues to have a lien in the Group 'C' post is also eligible, if otherwise eligible.
  • The parent Service/Cadre of the candidate must be a participating Service/Cadre of this examination.

Educational Qualification

  • Must have passed the 12th standard examination from a recognized Board or equivalent.

Typewriting Test Requirement

Candidates shall have to pass (if not already passed) one of the periodical typewriting tests in English or Hindi held by SSC:

Note: Candidates who do not pass the typewriting test within the probation period are liable to be reverted. Candidates declared permanently unfit for typewriting by a Civil Surgeon due to physical disability may be exempted in consultation with DoPT.

Selection Process – SSC JSA LDC DoPT LDCE 2025 Exam Pattern

The SSC JSA LDC LDCE 2025 selection process consists of a single-stage Computer Based Examination (CBE) of 180 marks and 3 hours duration. There is no interview or skill test at the selection stage. Final merit is determined solely on the basis of aggregate performance in the CBE, and the Commission prepares a Select List in order of merit up to the number of vacancies.

Part-I: Computer Based Examination (CBE) – Exam Pattern

Subject Number of Questions Maximum Marks
Comprehension / General English 60 60
General Knowledge 60 60
CSMOP (Central Secretariat Manual of Office Procedure) 60 60
Total 180 180
  • Duration: 3 hours (4 hours for candidates eligible for scribe)
  • Question Type: Objective type, Multiple Choice
  • Negative Marking: 0.25 marks deducted for each wrong answer
  • Medium: Candidates must attempt in the language (English/Hindi) opted in the application form, except the "General English" section which must be attempted in English
  • No Braille Question Paper: There is no Question Paper in Braille for Visually Handicapped candidates
  • Exam Centre: Delhi-NCR only
  • Compensatory Time: 20 minutes per hour for candidates eligible for scribe/assistive devices

Syllabus for Computer Based Examination
