Comprehension (English/Hindi) and General English Simple composition, Applied Grammar
General Knowledge Current events, everyday observation, general information about India
CSMOP Simple questions from Chapter No. 5, 6, and 10 of the latest CSMOP — Management of Dak Receipts, File Management System, Records Management

Tie-Breaking Rules

When two or more candidates secure equal aggregate marks, the tie is resolved in the following order:

  1. Marks obtained in 'Comprehension and General English' subject of CBE
  2. Marks obtained in 'General Knowledge' subject of CBE
  3. Date of birth — older candidate ranked higher
  4. Alphabetical order of names

Select List Preparation

After the examination, names of finally selected candidates will be arranged by SSC in order of merit. Selected candidates will be recommended for inclusion in the Select List for JSA/LDC Grade of CSCS Cadre up to the required number of vacancies. This is a competitive examination — success does not confer an automatic right to selection unless the cadre authority also confirms suitability based on conduct in service.

SSC JSA LDC DoPT LDCE 2025 Apply Online – Step-by-Step Process

The SSC JSA LDC DoPT LDCE 2025 apply online process is available exclusively at https://ssc.gov.in. This is a two-part process — One-Time Registration (OTR) followed by the Online Application Form. After submission, eligible candidates must also ensure their department forwards the printed hard copy to SSC Northern Region by 23 July 2026. Only applications forwarded by the Head of Department/Head of Office will be considered for admission.

  1. One-Time Registration (OTR) on the NEW SSC website: If you have not yet completed OTR on https://ssc.gov.in, do so first. OTR done on the old website (ssc.nic.in) is NOT valid for the new portal. Keep ready: mobile number, email ID, Aadhaar number (or Voter ID/PAN/Passport/Driving License), and Matriculation (10th class) board/roll number/year of passing. Opt for Aadhaar-Based Authentication for smoother processing. Complete OTR registration within 14 days of starting, or data will be deleted. Save your Registration Number and password.
  2. Log in and apply for the examination: Visit https://ssc.gov.in, log in with your Registration Number and password, click "Apply" under the JSA/LDC LDCE 2025 (CSCS, DoPT) listing in the "Live Exam" section.
  3. Fill the Online Application Form: Personal details (S. No. 1–18) auto-populate from OTR. Fill in cadre (Central Secretariat Clerical Service, DoPT), examination year (2025), joining date of feeder service/cadre, length of service, exam medium (English or Hindi), ministry/department/office details, Head of Department and Head of Office details, and complete service history in chronological order.
  4. Upload photograph (live capture) and signature: Capture a live photograph directly through the application module — no pre-existing photograph is required. Ensure plain background, good lighting, no cap/mask/glasses. Upload scanned signature in JPEG format (10–20 KB), dimensions approx. 6.0 cm (width) × 2.0 cm (height). Blurred or miniature signatures lead to rejection.
  5. Upload required certificates: Upload the following in PDF/JPEG format: (i) Service Book first page certified true copy attested by HoD/HoO; (ii) Certified particulars of service (posts held, pay scale, capacity); (iii) Educational qualification certificate (12th standard or equivalent); (iv) Disability certificate (PwBD candidates only).
  6. Preview, declare, and submit: Use the Preview option to verify all entries. Check photograph and signature compliance. Click "I Agree" on the declaration and submit. On successful submission, take a printout of the application form.
  7. Forward hard copy through department (mandatory): Print the submitted application form and attach self-attested photocopies of supporting documents. Submit to your Head of Department/Head of Office for forwarding to: The Regional Director, Staff Selection Commission (Northern Region), Block No.12, C.G.O. Complex, Lodhi Road, New Delhi – 110003, so as to reach by 23 July 2026 at 6:00 PM (or 30 July 2026 for candidates abroad/Andaman & Nicobar/Lakshadweep).
  8. Download Admit Card: Admission Certificate (AC) will be uploaded on the SSC-NR website (https://sscnr.nic.in) approximately 10 days before the exam; available for download 3–4 days before the exam. AC will NOT be sent by post.

Important: Only applications forwarded by the Head of Department/Head of Office will be considered. Candidates are advised to submit to their department well before the closing date to ensure timely forwarding. Applications received after the closing date at SSC will be summarily rejected.

Documents Required – Upload Checklist & Hard Copy Submission

Candidates applying for the SSC LDC JSA LDCE 2025 DoPT must upload the following documents at the time of online application and also include self-attested photocopies with the printed application forwarded by the department. All documents must be clear and legible; no original documents should be submitted at this stage.

Documents to Upload Online (and attach with hard copy)

  • Certified true copy of first page of Service Book duly attested by Head of Department/Head of Office — showing name, father's name, husband's name (if applicable), nationality, SC/ST details (if applicable), date of birth in Christian Era (figures and words)
  • Certified particulars of service attested by HoD/HoO — showing posts held, scale of pay, and capacity (substantive/officiating/permanent/temporary)
  • Certificate of essential educational qualification (12th standard or equivalent), if applicable
  • Disability certificate (PwBD candidates) — as per Annexure-VII (Form-V) or Annexure-VIII (Form-VI for multiple disabilities) of the notification

Documents to Carry to Exam Centre

  • Hard copy of Admission Certificate (AC)
  • Departmental Identity Card (Original) issued by employer
  • At least one valid government-issued photo ID — Voter ID, Driving License, PAN Card, Passport, or any Central/State Government-issued photo ID card (for candidates who have not undergone Aadhaar-Based Authentication, also carry two recent passport-size colour photographs and an additional DOB proof)
  • If Photo ID does not show date of birth — carry Matriculation Certificate/Marks Sheet (issued by CBSE/ICSE/State Boards), Birth Certificate, or Category Certificate
  • PwBD candidates availing scribe/assistive devices — carry Medical Certificate (Annexure-II or III) and scribe's photo ID proof (original and photocopy)

Departmental Forwarding Certificate – Role of Head of Department

A unique feature of the SSC JSA LDC DoPT LDCE 2025 is the mandatory role of the Head of Department or Head of Office in the application process. The forwarding authority must certify the candidate's service particulars, verify eligibility, sign and stamp the photograph on the printed application, and forward it to SSC Northern Region by the deadline. Without this forwarding, no application will be considered.

The Head of Department/Office must certify the following key points (as per Annexure-VI of the notification):

  • All information given by the candidate is verified and correct as per service records
  • The candidate belongs to the SC/ST community (if claimed), as verified from service records
  • No circumstance renders the candidate unsuitable for promotion to JSA/LDC of CSCS Cadre, DoPT
  • The candidate is a regularly appointed temporary/permanent Group 'C' employee of the participating Ministry/Department/Organization
  • The candidate fulfills all eligibility conditions for the year 2025 considering the crucial date and length of service
  • The candidate has not been debarred or disqualified by any Public Service Commission/SSC/Subordinate Service Commission for any examination/selection
  • A vacancy in the appropriate category is available in the Department/Organization

Critical: The forwarding authority must also sign the candidate's photograph on the printed application form and put a half-seal on the photograph and half on the form. Without this, the application will be summarily rejected.

PwBD / Scribe Provisions – SSC JSA LDC LDCE 2025

Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) applying for the SSC JSA LDC DoPT LDCE 2025 can avail the facility of scribe, technology, or assistive devices. The eligibility for scribe assistance depends on the nature and percentage of disability. Compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour of examination will be provided to all candidates eligible for scribe assistance — whether or not they actually avail the facility.

  • Blindness and Cerebral Palsy (40%+): Scribe/technology/assistive devices provided on request in the application form, with upload of disability certificate.
  • Other PwBD categories: Scribe provided on production of a certificate from Chief Medical Officer/Civil Surgeon/Medical Superintendent of a Government health institution (as per Annexure-II) confirming physical limitation to write.
  • PwD with less than 40% disability having difficulty writing: Scribe provided as per OM No. 29-6/2019-DD-III dated 10.08.2022, on production of certificate as per Annexure-III.
  • Scribe/assistive device facility must be opted for in the online application form — it will not be provided without prior intimation.

Common Mistakes to Avoid – SSC JSA LDC LDCE 2025 DoPT Application

This is a departmental exam with additional procedural requirements not seen in open competitive exams. Many candidates lose their application due to easily avoidable errors. Here are the most critical mistakes to watch for in the SSC JSA LDC CSCS DoPT LDCE 2025:

  1. Using old SSC website OTR for the new website: OTR generated on the old website (ssc.nic.in) is NOT valid on the new website (ssc.gov.in). Candidates must generate a fresh OTR on the new portal. Using old OTR credentials leads to failure to apply.
  2. Not completing OTR within 14 days: If you start OTR registration but do not complete it within 14 days, your data is automatically deleted. Start and complete OTR well before the application deadline.
  3. Submitting multiple applications: Only ONE application should be submitted. Multiple applications may lead to rejection of the entire candidature.
  4. Not ensuring the department forwards the hard copy on time: Many candidates submit the online application correctly but forget that the department must also forward the printed hard copy to SSC NR by 23 July 2026. Applications received late at SSC — even with valid online submissions — are summarily rejected. Inform your department immediately after applying online.
  5. Forwarding authority not signing the photograph: The Head of Department/Office must personally sign the candidate's photo on the printed application form and put a half-seal across the photo. Without this, the application is summarily rejected — no appeal entertained.
  6. Uploading a photograph of a pre-existing photograph: The application module captures a live photograph. Candidates who photograph a pre-existing printed photo (instead of taking a live capture) will have their applications rejected summarily.
  7. Wearing glasses, cap, or mask in the live photograph: Candidates are specifically instructed not to wear any of these while capturing the live photo. Similarly, the appearance at the exam should match the application photo — changed appearances may deny entry.
  8. Uploading a miniature or blurred signature: The signature must be in JPEG format (10–20 KB), approximately 6.0 cm × 2.0 cm, occupying at least 80% of the signature box. Miniature or blurred signatures are a leading cause of application rejection.
  9. Not indicating the correct medium of examination: Candidates must choose English or Hindi as the medium in the application. The General English section must be attempted in English regardless of medium chosen. This choice cannot be changed after submission.
  10. Changing appearance significantly between application and exam day: Since the exam centre staff verifies appearance against the application photo, significant changes (beard, haircut, spectacles) may raise suspicion and lead to not being allowed to appear.

SSC ASO Apply Online 2026 – Step-by-Step Process

The SSC ASO Apply Online 2026 process involves two stages: One Time Registration (OTR) on the SSC portal, followed by filling the actual examination application. Candidates who had registered on the old website (ssc.nic.in) must create a fresh OTR on the new website (ssc.gov.in) as the old OTR is not functional on the new portal.

  1. Visit the official SSC website: https://ssc.gov.in
  2. Click on "Register Now" under the Login or Register section to complete One Time Registration (OTR) if not already done on the new website.
  3. During OTR, opt for Aadhaar-Based Authentication as advised by the Commission.
  4. After OTR is complete, log in using your Registration Number and password.
  5. Click the "Apply" link under "Assistant Section Officer / Assistant Grade Limited Departmental Competitive Examination, 2025" in the Live Exam tab.
  6. Fill in departmental details - select your Cadre/Service, joining date of feeder service, and length of service.
  7. Capture a live photograph using webcam/smartphone as prompted (no pre-existing photo allowed).
  8. Upload your scanned signature in JPEG format (10–20 KB, dimensions: 6 cm × 2 cm).
  9. Upload mandatory documents including certified true copy of Service Book (first page) and particulars of service. PwBD candidates must also upload their disability certificate.
  10. Review all entries in the Preview section, accept the declaration, and click Submit Application.
  11. Take a printout of the submitted application form.
  12. Submit the printed copy along with all required documents through your Head of Department / Head of Office to SSC (NR), New Delhi, by 23 July 2026.

Important: Only those candidates whose application is forwarded by their Head of Department / Head of Office will be considered for admission to this examination. Applications submitted directly without departmental forwarding will be rejected.

SSC ASO Exam Pattern 2026 – Scheme of Examination

The SSC Assistant Section Officer Exam 2026 is conducted in two parts. Part-I is a Computer Based Examination (CBE) carrying 300 marks, and Part-II involves Evaluation of Service Records (APARs) carrying 100 marks. The final merit is prepared on the combined aggregate of both parts. There is no separate qualifying exam - this is a competitive examination.

Part-I: Computer Based Examination (300 Marks)

Paper Subjects Type Max. Marks Duration
Paper-I (i) General Awareness – flagship programmes and GoI initiatives
(ii) Constitutional provisions and their general application in GoI
(iii) Parliamentary procedures (Manual of Parliamentary Procedures, MoPA instructions)
(iv) Reading Comprehension in English / Hindi
(v) Central Secretariat – Manual of Office Procedure
(vi) Allocation of Business Rules and Transaction of Business Rules
(vii) Noting and Drafting		 Objective (MCQ) 150 3 hours (4 hours for eligible scribe candidates)

(ii) Financial Rules – TA, LTC
(iii) Legislations – RTI Act 2005, POSH Act 2013
(iv) Records Management
(v) Précis Writing		 Objective (MCQ) 150 3 hours (4 hours for eligible scribe candidates)

There is a negative marking of 0.25 marks (25%) for each wrong answer in both Paper-I and Paper-II. Candidates must attempt the examination only in the language (English or Hindi) opted in the application form. There will be no question paper in Braille.

Part-II: Evaluation of Record of Service (100 Marks)

One hundred marks are reserved for evaluation of Annual Performance Appraisal Reports (APARs). Candidates shortlisted based on their Part-I aggregate performance will proceed to Part-II. Marks from Part-II will be added to determine the final rank. Once APARs have been evaluated, no request for change in APAR grading will be entertained.

SSC ASO Selection Process 2026

The SSC ASO selection process 2026 is a two-stage merit-based system. Candidates must clear the Computer Based Examination before their service records are evaluated. Final selection is strictly based on combined merit - no candidate has a right to selection merely by passing the exam.

  1. Stage 1 – Computer Based Examination (Part-I): Paper-I and Paper-II, each of 150 marks. The Commission may fix minimum qualifying marks individually for each paper.
  2. Stage 2 – APAR Evaluation (Part-II): Only candidates who qualify Part-I are eligible. Service records (APARs) are evaluated for 100 marks.
  3. Final Merit: Aggregate of Part-I (300 marks) + Part-II (100 marks) = 400 marks total. Names of finally selected candidates will be arranged in order of merit separately for each cadre.

Tie-Breaking Rules

In case of equal aggregate marks, ties are resolved in the following order: (i) Marks in Paper-I, (ii) Marks in Paper-II, (iii) Date of birth - older candidate ranked higher, (iv) Alphabetical order of names.

Common Mistakes to Avoid – SSC ASO Apply Online 2026

Based on typical departmental exam application processes, candidates should be especially careful about the following errors that frequently lead to rejection or disqualification.

  • Using Old SSC OTR: OTR created on the old website (ssc.nic.in) will not work on ssc.gov.in. Candidates must create a new OTR on the new website before applying.
  • Not forwarding hard copy through HoD/HoO: Online submission alone is not enough. The printed application must be forwarded by the Head of Department or Head of Office and must reach SSC NR by 23 July 2026. Failure to do this renders the application void.
  • Uploading pre-existing photographs: The portal requires a live photograph captured at the time of application. Uploading a pre-existing photo will lead to summary rejection.
  • Miniature or blurred signatures: Signatures must occupy at least 80% of the signature box and must be clear. Miniature signatures are the most common reason for rejection.
  • Mismatch in personal details: Name, date of birth, father's name, and mother's name in the application must exactly match the Matriculation certificate. Any discrepancy can cancel your candidature.
  • Submitting multiple applications: Only one application is allowed per candidate. Multiple submissions may lead to rejection of all applications.
  • Not verifying service eligibility before applying: Candidates must confirm they have completed six years of approved service in the feeder grade as on 01 July 2025 before applying.
  • Changing appearance before the exam: The appearance on exam day must match the photograph in the application form. Examination staff may deny entry to candidates with noticeably different appearances.
  • Carrying electronic devices: Mobile phones, Bluetooth devices, or any electronic gadget in the examination hall attracts a debarment of 3–5 years.

RCF Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria – Qualification and Age Limit

The eligibility criteria for RCF Officer Recruitment 2026 vary significantly by post and grade. All qualifications must be from UGC/AICTE-recognized universities or institutions, and experience is calculated as of 01 March 2026.

Officer (Finance) – E1 Grade

Candidates must hold either a CA/CMA qualification or a full-time graduation degree in Commerce/Accounting/Finance (B.Com, BMS, BAF, BBA) along with a 2-year full-time MBA/MMS/PGDM/PGDBM with specialization in Finance. M.Com alone is not accepted. Minimum 60% in the final year of the qualifying post-graduation degree is required (55% for SC/ST). No percentage criterion applies for CA/CMA holders. Minimum 2 years of post-qualification executive-level experience in accounting, auditing, budgeting, or taxation is required. Training, internship, and articleship periods do not count toward experience. Age limit: SC/ST – 39 years; OBC (NCL) – 37 years as on 01.03.2026.

Officer (HR) – E1 Grade

A full-time graduation degree in any discipline plus a 2-year full-time post-graduation degree/diploma/equivalent master's degree with specialization in HR/Personnel/Social Work/Welfare/Industrial Relations/Labour Studies from a UGC/AICTE institution is required. Minimum 55% for SC category candidates in the final year of the post-graduation. Additional qualification in law and proficiency in Marathi are preferred. Minimum 2 years of experience in HR departments covering labour administration, industrial relations, and grievance handling is required. Age limit: SC – 39 years as on 01.03.2026.

Officer (Medical) – E1 Grade

MBBS with completed internship and registration with the Medical Council of India or State Medical Council is mandatory. Preference is given to candidates with a Certificate Course in Industrial Health (3 months) or AFIH recognized by DGFASLI, or a 2-year recognized Diploma in Anaesthesiology. Minimum 2 years of experience (excluding internship) in a hospital of 25 beds or more is required. Age limit: OBC (NCL) – 37 years as on 01.03.2026.

Senior Manager (CC Lab) – E5 Grade

Candidates must hold either a Ph.D. in Chemistry from a UGC/AICTE-approved institution or a 4-year full-time B.E./B.Tech in Chemical Engineering/Petrochemical Engineering/Chemical Technology (minimum 60% aggregate). Preference is given to Ph.D. holders. Minimum 17 years of relevant experience in academics or research is required. Age limit: OBC (NCL) – 52 years as on 01.03.2026.

Officer (Legal) – E1 Grade

A regular full-time LLB degree or a 5-year integrated Law degree from a recognized Indian university is required, with a minimum of 60% in the final year of LLB. Common Mistakes to Avoid – RCF Bharti 2026

Many candidates lose their eligibility due to avoidable errors in the application process. The following original guidance is based on common pitfalls in PSU recruitment applications.

Uploading documents in wrong formats is one of the most common rejection reasons - ensure photographs are in JPG/JPEG at 165×125 pixels and all supporting documents are in PDF format. Eligibility Criteria - Qualification & Age Limit

The CCRUM Ayush Job 2026 eligibility varies significantly by post group. Candidates should verify their qualification carefully against the specific post before applying, as merely meeting one criterion is not sufficient.

Group A - Research Officers

Research Officer (Unani): PG Degree (MD or MS) in Unani System of Medicine from a university/institution recognized by NCISM (formerly CCIM), plus enrolment on the Central Registrar of NCISM/CCIM or State Register of Unani/ISM. Age: up to 40 years (Government servants get 5 years' relaxation).

Research Officer (Pathology): MD in Pathology from an MCI-recognized university. Enrolment on Central Register of MCI or State Register of Medical Council. Age: up to 40 years.

Research Officer (Physiology): Master's Degree in Molecular Biology / Biotechnology / Human Genetics / Genetics Engineering from a recognized institution, plus 3 years' post-Master's research experience OR a Ph.D. in the relevant subject. Age: up to 40 years.

Group B - Key Posts

Asst. Research Officer (Pharmacology): M.Sc. in Pharmacology or M.V.Sc from a recognized university. Age: up to 30 years.

Asst. Research Officer (Pharmacognosy/Botany): Master's Degree in the concerned discipline plus 3 years' research/teaching experience OR a Ph.D. in the relevant discipline. Age: up to 35 years.

Staff Nurse: B.Sc. (Hons) Nursing / Regular B.Sc. Nursing / Post-Basic B.Sc. Nursing OR Diploma in General Nursing & Midwifery from a recognized institution, registered as Nurse/Nurse & Midwife with State Nursing Council, plus 1 year's experience in a minimum 50-bed hospital. Age: up to 35 years.

Accounts Officer (HQ): Degree from a recognized university plus 3 years' experience in Cash, Accounts, and Budget work in a Government Office / PSU / Autonomous Body. Age: up to 30 years (5-year relaxation for CCRUM employees).

MLT: Bachelor's Degree in Medical Laboratory Science with 2 years' relevant experience. Age: up to 35 years.

Library & Information Assistant: Degree from a recognized university plus Degree in Library Science. Age: up to 28 years.

Group C - Key Posts

UDC: Degree from a recognized university. Age: between 18 and 27 years.

LDC: 12th class pass with typing speed of 35 wpm in English or 30 wpm in Hindi on computer. Age: between 18 and 27 years.

Stenographer Grade-III: Matric/equivalent plus shorthand speed of 80 wpm and typewriting speed of 40 wpm. Age: up to 28 years.

Staff Car Driver: Matriculation pass, valid driving license for Motor Cars/LMV, 3 years' motor car driving experience, knowledge of vehicle maintenance. Age: between 18 and 25 years.

MTS: Matriculation/equivalent pass OR ITI pass in relevant subject. Age: between 18 and 25 years.

Compounder: Matric or equivalent plus Certificate of Training as Compounder in Unani System of Medicine (minimum 1 year), plus 2 years' experience preferably in a Unani Dispensary/Hospital. Age: 28 years and below.

Pharmacist: 10+2 with Science plus 2-year Diploma in Pharmacy plus registration with State/Central Pharmacy Council. Age: between 18 and 25 years.

Age Relaxation Summary

Candidates wondering about age relaxation can note the following: SC/ST candidates get 5 years' relaxation, OBC-NCL candidates get 3 years, PwBD (UR) candidates get 10 years, PwBD (OBC-NCL) candidates get 13 years, and PwBD (SC/ST) candidates get 15 years. The maximum age after all cumulative relaxations shall not exceed 56 years. Candidates domiciled in Jammu & Kashmir between 1 January 1980 and 31 December 1989 are also eligible for 5 years' relaxation.

Application Fee - CCRUM Recruitment 2026

The CCRUM 2026 application fee structure is divided into a non-refundable Processing Fee (applicable to all candidates) and an Examination Fee (waived for exempted categories). SC/ST, PwBD, EWS, Women candidates, and Ex-Servicemen are exempt from the Examination Fee but must still pay the Processing Fee.

Payment is accepted only through the online payment gateway via Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, or UPI. Cash, Demand Draft, and Postal Orders are not accepted. The fee is inclusive of GST; bank charges will be levied additionally depending on the payment mode.

Selection Process - CCRUM Ayush Vacancy 2026

The CCRUM 2026 selection process differs by post group. Group A candidates face both a written test and an interview, while Group B and C candidates are selected primarily through the Computer Based Test.

Group A Posts (Research Officers):

  • Online CBT - 70 marks (subject knowledge + research methodology + general awareness)
  • Interview - 30 marks
  • Shortlisting ratio: 1:5 for 1 vacancy, 1:4 for 2 vacancies, 1:3 for 3 or more vacancies
  • Minimum qualifying marks: 25% for SC/ST/PwBD; 30% for all others

Group B & C Posts:

  • Online CBT - 100 marks
  • Skill Test (mandatory and qualifying) for LDC, Stenographer Grade-III, Staff Car Driver, and wherever applicable
  • Minimum qualifying marks: 25% for SC/ST/PwBD; 30% for all others

Negative Marking: There is a 0.25 mark deduction per wrong answer in the CBT for all posts except MTS, where there is no negative marking.

Exam Duration: 100 minutes for all candidates (Group A, B & C). PwBD candidates eligible for a scribe receive 130 minutes (100 + 30 compensatory minutes).

Exam Centers: New Delhi/Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai, Mumbai, Hyderabad, and Guwahati.

Tie-Breaking Rules: In case of equal marks, tie-breaking follows this order: older age ranked higher → higher subject marks → higher marks in second part of syllabus → earlier degree/diploma completion → higher final aggregate percentage.

Exam Syllabus at a Glance

The CCRUM CBT syllabus is post-specific. Every paper follows a common structure: subject knowledge (70 marks) + research methodology/relevant technical knowledge (20 marks) + general awareness/IT & computing (10 marks) for Group B and C posts. Group A post papers total 70 marks (subject: 40 + research methodology: 20 + general awareness/IT: 10), followed by an interview of 30 marks. MTS and Staff Car Driver follow SSC's MTS/Matric-level examination syllabus.

How to Apply - CCRUM Recruitment 2026 Online Application

All applications for CCRUM Bharti 2026 must be submitted online only through the official CCRUM website. No documents or application forms need to be sent to CCRUM by post or mail.

  1. Visit www.ccrum.res.in or www.ccrum.ayush.gov.in and go to the "Advertisement/Vacancy" tab.
  2. Create a new account (Step I): Enter your full name (as per Matriculation Certificate), father's name, mother's name, gender, date of birth, mobile number, valid email ID, and Government ID proof. Verify via OTP.
  3. Complete your profile (Step II): Log in with your Reference Number and Password. Upload photograph, signature, caste certificate, disability certificate (if applicable), basic qualification certificates, and other relevant documents.
  4. Apply for the post (Step III): Select the post(s) you wish to apply for, fill in post-specific information, and upload post-specific documents.
  5. Pay the fee: You will be redirected to the payment gateway. Pay via Debit Card, Credit Card, Net Banking, or UPI. Download the payment acknowledgement slip.
  6. Download your application form in PDF format from the Dashboard for future reference.

Important: Details entered during account creation (Step I) cannot be modified at any later stage. Candidates applying for multiple posts must use the same login reference number and pay the fee separately for each post.

Modification Window

After the application window closes, CCRUM provides a Modification Window from 3 August 2026 (10:00 AM) to 5 August 2026 (23:59 hrs). A modification fee of ₹300 per attempt per post is charged. Note that account creation details from Step I cannot be changed through this window. If a modification makes a candidate ineligible for the post, the change will not be permitted.

Salary / Pay Scale

The CCRUM Recruitment 2026 offers 7th CPC pay structure with NPA (Non-Practising Allowance) for Group A medical posts as per Government of India rules. Selected candidates are placed on probation for two years, extendable at the discretion of the competent authority, and will be governed by the New Pension Scheme (NPS). All posts carry All India transfer liability; candidates must be willing to serve at any of CCRUM's 24 Institutes/Centers across India.

Post Group Pay Level Pay Range
Group A (Research Officers) Pay Level-10 ₹56,100 – ₹1,77,500 + NPA
Group B (ARO, Staff Nurse, AO) Pay Level-7 ₹44,900 – ₹1,42,400
Group B (Research Asst., MLT, LIA, etc.) Pay Level-6 ₹35,400 – ₹1,12,400
Group C (Pharmacist, Social Worker) Pay Level-5 ₹29,200 – ₹92,300
Group C (Compounder, Steno, UDC) Pay Level-4 ₹25,500 – ₹81,100
Group C (LDC, Staff Car Driver) Pay Level-2 ₹19,900 – ₹63,200
Group C (MTS) Pay Level-1 ₹18,000 – ₹56,900

Documents Required

Candidates should keep the following documents ready before starting the CCRUM online application 2026. All documents must be scanned and uploaded in JPEG/JPG or PDF format as specified.

  • Latest passport-size colour photograph (50–100 KB, JPEG/JPG), taken in 2026
  • Signature on white paper with black ink pen (50–100 KB, JPG/JPEG)
  • Caste/Category Certificate in Central Government format (SC/ST/OBC/PwBD/EWS)
  • Disability Certificate issued by Competent Authority (for PwBD candidates)
  • Discharge Certificate (for Ex-Servicemen)
  • Educational qualification certificates with mark sheets
  • Valid Government photo ID proof (Voter ID, Passport, PAN Card, or Driving License)
  • No Objection Certificate (for candidates already in Government service)
  • Each document file: between 100 KB and 1000 KB in PDF/JPG/JPEG format

Common Mistakes to Avoid

These are avoidable errors that frequently lead to rejection or disqualification in CCRUM recruitment:

  • Entering wrong details at account creation: Name, date of birth, and gender entered at Step I cannot be changed under any circumstances. Cross-check with your Matriculation Certificate before submitting.
  • Not checking the OBC certificate date: Your OBC (NCL) certificate must have been obtained within 3 years before the closing date of application. An outdated certificate will result in disqualification.
  • Applying through offline modes: Applications submitted by post, email, or courier are rejected outright without any communication.
  • Uploading blurry or cut documents: All uploaded documents must be clear, complete, and within the specified file size limits.
  • Missing the payment confirmation step: Your application is only considered submitted after successful payment. Always ensure the payment status reads "Payment Received."
  • Not downloading your application form: After Step III, download and preserve your application form PDF and payment receipt from the Dashboard for future reference.
  • Using electronic devices in the exam hall: Mobiles, smart watches, calculators, earphones, and Bluetooth devices are strictly prohibited. Violation leads to a ban of at least 5 years from CCRUM exams.
  • Applying for multiple posts with different logins: Candidates must use the same reference number for all posts. Creating multiple accounts is not permitted.

Age Limit – Indian Navy Officer Recruitment 2026

The Indian Navy officer age limit 2026 varies by branch. Refer to the vacancy table above for branch-specific date-of-birth ranges. All candidates must be unmarried at the time of applying. The selected candidates will be inducted in the rank of Sub Lieutenant.

Who Can Apply?

  • Candidates who have obtained a graduate/post-graduate degree or are in the final year.
  • Degree must be from a university incorporated by an Act of Central or State Legislature in India, or other institutions established by Act of Parliament or deemed to be Universities/Autonomous Universities under UGC Act 1956, IIT Act 1961, AICTE Act 1987, NITSER Act 2007, IIT Act 2014.
  • Candidates studying in the possession of a degree from foreign institutions may also apply for any Branch/Cadre as enumerated above, with an equivalence certificate of the degree from UGC.

Also read: AIIMS CRE-5 Recruitment 2026: Apply Online for 1484 Group B & C Posts Across 28 Central Govt Institutes

Indian Navy SSC Selection Process 2026

The Indian Navy SSC selection process 2026 is a multi-stage procedure that begins with shortlisting based on normalised marks and culminates in a merit list after SSB interview and medical examination. Understanding each stage will help candidates prepare strategically for this defence government job.

Stage 1 – Shortlisting for SSB Interview

Shortlisting will be done using formulae mentioned on the Indian Navy website (https://www.joinindiannavy.gov.in/files/normalisation.pdf). Marks obtained by candidates in the qualifying degree will be considered for SSB shortlisting.

  • BE/B.Tech candidates: Marks obtained up to the fifth semester will be considered. For candidates in the final year, shortlisting will be based on final-year performance.
  • Post-Graduate Degree Programme candidates: For those who have completed MSc, MCA, MBA, M.Tech, marks obtained in all semesters will be considered.

Stage 2 – SSB Interview

Shortlisted candidates will be informed about their selection for SSB interview through e-mail or SMS. Candidates are advised not to change their e-mail/mobile number till selection process is over and to check their inbox and spam folder periodically. Change of SSB Centre for interview is not permissible under any circumstances.

Stage 3 – Medical Examination

SSB-recommended candidates will be required to inform their final result of their respective degree to the Indian Navy at [email protected] prior to 20 June 2027. Candidates declared fit in the medical examination would be appointed as per availability of vacancies in the entry.

Stage 4 – Merit List

A merit list will be prepared based on SSB marks for all entries, after medical clearance for the respective entry. Mere inclusion in the select list does not confer a vested right to appointment. All vacancies are to be filled as per service requirement and as per statutory guidelines issued from time to time.

Indian Navy Officer Salary 2026

One of the most frequently searched topics for this recruitment is the Indian Navy officer salary 2026. Selected candidates will be inducted in the rank of Sub Lieutenant. Here are the key pay and allowance details as mentioned in the official notification:

  • The initial gross salary of a Sub Lieutenant starts from Rs 1,20,000/- (approximately) per month, along with other allowances as applicable.
  • Pilot/NAOO and Submarine allowance of Rs 31,250/- will be admissible to candidates post successful completion of training.
  • Further details on pay, allowances, Group Insurance and Gratuity/Leave Entitlements/Duties of Officers are available on the Indian Navy website at www.joinindiannavy.gov.in.

Calculate your exact in-hand Salary in 10 seconds - Calculate Now

Tenure of Commission

Selected candidates will be granted Short Service Commission initially for 12 years, extendable by a maximum of 02 years, subject to service requirement, performance, medical eligibility, and willingness of candidates.

Indian Navy SSC Probation Period

Probation period for all branches/cadres is two years. The probation period will commence from the date of grant of the rank of Sub Lieutenant and will terminate after two years or on completion of initial training (whichever is later). During probation, officers are liable to be discharged in case of unsatisfactory performance at any stage.

Also read: SSC SSA/UDC LDCE 2025 Notification Out - Apply Online for 227 Group C Posts

Indian Navy Physical and Medical Standards 2026

Candidates are strongly advised to ascertain their eligibility for branches with respect to applicable medical standards, prior to indicating their preference. This is especially relevant for SSC (Pilot) entry where specified numbers of candidates based on service requirement will be considered for SSB/CPSS/Aviation Medical Examination.

  • A specified number of candidates for SSC (Pilot) entry will be considered for SSB/CPSS/Aviation Medical Examination and are advised to check physical/medical standards (Height, leg length etc.) before selecting this option.
  • Remaining candidates will be considered for other preferences opted by them.
  • Candidates declared medically fit for DG Jul 27 course will be considered fit for all SSC branches of IN (except for Pilot/NAOO).
  • Please visit www.joinindiannavy.gov.in for information. SSB-recommended candidates must undergo medical examination applicable to their entry. Change of medical hospital/centre is not permissible under any circumstances.

Training Details – Indian Naval Academy

Candidates selected for the Indian Navy SSC Jun 2027 (AT 27) Course will undergo training at the Indian Naval Academy (INA), Ezhimala, Kerala. Key training-related points are as follows:

  • Candidates will be inducted in the rank of Sub Lieutenant, subject to clearing induction medical examination at INA, Ezhimala upon posting.
  • Only unmarried candidates are eligible for training. Any candidate found to be married or who marries during training will be discharged from service.
  • Candidates must fulfil the educational qualification stipulated above before joining INA, Ezhimala by June 2027. The candidate failing to meet stipulated educational criteria will not be permitted to join INA, Ezhimala.
  • Male candidates shortlisted for GS(X) are also eligible to volunteer for submarine arm subject to medical fitness, vacancies, and service requirements.

Apply Online – Indian Navy SSC Officer 2026

Candidates who meet the Indian Navy SSC eligibility criteria 2026 can apply online through the official Indian Navy recruitment portal. The online application process is active from 25 June 2026 and the final deadline is 27 July 2026. No applications will be accepted after the last date.

Important instructions before applying:

  • Candidates must register and fill the application on the Indian Navy website at www.joinindiannavy.gov.in. To save time, candidates can fill in their details and upload documents in advance.
  • Whilst filling the e-application, keep the following documents readily available:
    • Correct personal particulars (as given in Matriculation Certificate)
    • Valid e-mail address and mobile number (mandatory fields)
    • CGPA covering up to 5th & 7th semester for regular and integrated BE/B.Tech courses respectively and all semesters for other degree programmes
    • All relevant documents (preferably mark sheets up to 10th & 12th certificate)
    • Date of birth proof (as proof of 10th or 12th certificate)
    • NCC 'C' certificate issued by National Cadet Corps (if applicable)
    • Recent passport-size colour photograph in original JPG/TIFF format
  • If any scanned document is not legible/readable, the application will be rejected. Candidates must take a printout of the application and carry it while appearing for SSB interview.
  • The application once submitted will be final and no request for amendments/change will be entertained.
  • Multiple applications for this course by any candidate will lead to cancellation of his/her candidature.

Indian Navy SSC Officer 2026 Apply Online Link: Apply Here

Common Application Mistakes to Avoid

Many candidates make avoidable errors while applying for defence jobs in India 2026. Based on general guidance for government online application processes, here are common mistakes to be careful about:

  • Uploading blurred, low-resolution, or incorrectly formatted photographs and documents - these lead to rejection.
  • Entering incorrect personal details that do not match your Matriculation Certificate.
  • Selecting a branch for which you do not meet the educational qualification or stream requirement.
  • Failing to include CGPA/marks for all required semesters as specified for your course type.
  • Changing your registered mobile number or e-mail address after submission - you may miss SSB shortlisting communications.
  • Submitting multiple application forms - this will lead to cancellation of candidature.
  • Not taking a printout of the submitted application - candidates must carry it to the SSB interview.

Selection Process for Anganwadi Recruitment 2026

There is no written examination for Anganwadi Worker and Helper posts. Selection is merit-based on academic qualifications. For Supervisor and CDPO posts, a written exam or interview may be conducted.

Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 – FAQ's

How to apply for Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 online?

Visit your state's official WCD / ICDS portal (link provided in table above). Register with mobile & Aadhaar, fill the application form, upload documents (photo, 10th certificate, Aadhaar, domicile), and submit before the last date. Print the application acknowledgement slip after submission.

What is the eligibility for Anganwadi Worker 2026?

Candidates must have passed 10th or 12th standard from a recognized board. Age limit is 18–35 years (varies by state). Must be a permanent resident of the ward/village for which vacancy exists. Only female candidates are eligible for Worker and Helper posts.

What is the salary of Anganwadi Worker in 2026?

Anganwadi Worker receives a monthly honorarium of ₹10,000–₹20,000 depending on the state (Karnataka and TN are highest at ~₹14,000). Anganwadi Helper gets ₹5,000–₹7,000/month. The Central Government pays ₹4,500/month as base honorarium, and states add their own component on top.

Is there a written exam for Anganwadi jobs?

No, there is no written examination for Anganwadi Worker and Anganwadi Helper posts. Selection is purely merit-based on academic qualification marks (10th / 12th percentage). For Supervisor / CDPO posts, a written exam or interview may be conducted depending on the state.

What is the age limit for Anganwadi Helper?

Age limit is 18 to 35 years as of 1st January 2026 in most states. SC/ST candidates get 5 years relaxation (maximum age 40). OBC candidates get 3 years relaxation (maximum age 38). PwD candidates get additional relaxation as per state rules.

What documents are required for Anganwadi job application?

Required documents: Aadhaar card, 10th/12th marksheet and certificate, domicile/residence certificate, caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC), passport-size photograph, scanned signature, and EWS/PwD certificate if applicable. Graduation certificate is needed for Supervisor post applications.

What is ICDS recruitment 2026?

ICDS stands for Integrated Child Development Services - the government programme under which Anganwadi centres operate nationwide. ICDS recruitment 2026 refers to hiring of Anganwadi Workers, Helpers, Supervisors, and CDPOs by state WCD departments under the Ministry of Women & Child Development (wcd.nic.in).

Is Anganwadi Worker a permanent government job?

Anganwadi Workers and Helpers are honorary workers, not regular government employees. They receive a fixed monthly honorarium (not salary) and are entitled to benefits like ESI, health insurance, and maternity benefits. Supervisors and CDPOs are regular government employees in most states and receive full pay & grade pay.

Can I apply for Anganwadi job from a different district?

No. Anganwadi Workers and Helpers must be permanent residents of the same ward/village/district where the vacancy exists. A domicile or residence certificate is mandatory. Applications from outside the specified locality are rejected. For Supervisor/CDPO posts, the same district residency rule generally applies.

Eligibility for Forest Department Jobs

Below is a general idea of qualification and age for popular posts like Forest Guard, Forester and Forest Range Officer. Candidates should always check the official notification for detailed eligibility criteria.

Education Qualification for Forest Guard, Forester, Ranger

  • Forest Guard / Field Guard / Forest Watcher / Beat Guard: Usually 10th pass or 12th pass from a recognized board, knowledge of local language, and basic physical standards as per state rules.
  • Forester / Section Forest Officer / Deputy Forest Ranger: Generally 12th pass or graduate in any stream or science-related subjects, with physical standards and sometimes driving or technical skills depending on the post.
  • Forest Range Officer (RFO) / Forest Ranger / ACF: Normally graduate degree in Science, Agriculture, Forestry, Environmental Science, Engineering or related disciplines, with higher physical standards and sometimes a competitive exam similar to state PCS level.
  • IFS / Indian Forest Service and senior posts (DCF, CF, CCF, PCCF): Filled through UPSC Indian Forest Service Examination and promotions, requiring a graduate degree and all-India competitive selection.

Age Limit & Relaxation

  • Forest Guard / Forester / Field Guard: Minimum age is usually 18 years and maximum age is around 27–30 years, with age relaxation for SC, ST, OBC, EWS, Ex-servicemen and other categories as per government rules.
  • Forest Range Officer / ACF and higher competitive posts: Age limit often ranges from 21 to 32 years (varies by recruitment), with relaxations for reserved categories.
  • Exact age limit, cut-off date and relaxation details always depend on the particular notification, so candidates should verify from the official advertisement before applying.

Selection Process & Exam Pattern

The selection process for Forest Department Jobs 2026 typically includes written examinations, physical tests and document verification. Some posts also conduct medical examination and walking tests due to the demanding nature of field duties.

Written Exam, PET/PST & Document Verification

  • Written Exam: Most Forest Guard, Forester and Forest Range Officer recruitments start with a written exam based on objective-type questions (MCQs).
  • PET / PST (Physical Efficiency Test / Physical Standard Test): Candidates who qualify written exam are called for running, walking test, height, chest measurement and other physical parameters as per post and gender.
  • Document Verification: Shortlisted candidates must produce original certificates of age, qualification, caste, residence, sports/NCC and other documents mentioned in the notification.
  • Medical Examination: Many forest posts require medical fitness to ensure candidates can perform field duties in forests, wildlife areas and difficult terrain.

Syllabus Highlights for Forest Guard & Ranger

Typical syllabus for written exam may include:

  • General Knowledge & Current Affairs (national, state-level, environment and forest-related topics)
  • General Hindi / English or regional language (grammar, comprehension, vocabulary)
  • General Mathematics / Quantitative Aptitude (up to 10th or 12th level)
  • General Science and Environmental Studies (forest, wildlife, biodiversity, conservation, climate, basic biology)
  • Reasoning Ability (logical and analytical reasoning)

Exact subject-wise marks, number of questions, negative marking and exam duration will be given in the respective forest department notification.

Two Types of No Exam Govt Jobs

No-exam recruitment in India falls into two patterns, and knowing which one a notification belongs to tells you exactly what to prepare for:

Type Typical Posts Who it's for How Selection Works
Fresher - no exam, usually no interview Apprentice, GDS, trainee 10th/12th/ITI/Diploma/Graduate pass Merit list prepared from academic marks
Experienced - no exam, interview-based Officer, manager, specialist, medical Professionals with relevant work experience Shortlisting based on qualification/experience, followed by a personal interview

How Recruitment Without Exam Works in Government Jobs

This section explains the different routes through which government departments fill vacancies without conducting a written competitive exam.

1. Direct Recruitment

Certain senior and specialised posts - such as Chairman, Member, and Secretary in Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and State Public Service Commissions (PSCs) - are filled through direct recruitment based on eligibility criteria like qualifications, experience, and domain expertise, rather than a written exam. Similarly, some administrative posts in the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) may be filled through direct recruitment.

2. Sports Quota Recruitment

Government organisations such as Indian Railways, the Indian Army, and Public Sector Banks reserve a quota of posts for candidates with outstanding achievements in sports at the state, national, or international level. Eligible candidates can be appointed to posts like Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, and Clerk without going through the regular written exam.

3. Cultural Quota Recruitment

Indian Railways also recruits individuals with exceptional talent in arts, fine arts, music, or literature under the cultural quota for posts such as Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, and Assistant Loco Pilot.

4. Internal Promotions and Deputation

Government departments, including the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and Indian Police Service (IPS), promote existing employees to higher posts based on performance, seniority, and experience - without requiring them to clear a fresh competitive exam. Ex-servicemen and defence personnel are also often considered for civilian government posts through deputation or reservation quotas, without a written exam.

5. Apprenticeships and Trainee Programmes

Railways, PSUs, and central organisations like DRDO and BEL regularly hire Act Apprentices, Trade Apprentices, and Project Trainees through merit lists based on academic marks - with no written entrance test.

6. Walk-in Interviews

Some government and PSU organisations directly call candidates for walk-in interviews based on their qualifications and experience, especially for technical, medical, and contractual roles.

Government Jobs Without Exam by Sector

This section breaks down no-exam opportunities by sector - banking and railways - which are among the most common areas where such recruitment occurs.

Bank Jobs Without Exam

While most public sector bank recruitment (PO, Clerk, SO) happens through IBPS or bank-specific written exams, some banks fill specific posts - such as Local Bank Officer and certain Specialist Officer roles - through direct recruitment, where the bank shortlists applications based on eligibility criteria and conducts an interview instead of a written test.

Railway Jobs Without Exam

Indian Railways and the various Railway Recruitment Boards/Cells (RRBs/RRCs) offer no-exam entry through:

  • Act Apprentices (selection via academic merit list)
  • Sports Quota posts (Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, Clerk)
  • Cultural Quota posts (Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, Assistant Loco Pilot)
  • Scouts and Guides Quota

Before You Apply: How to Spot Fake "No Exam" Job Offers

No-exam recruitment is the single biggest magnet for job fraud in India, because "direct joining, no exam" is exactly what scammers promise. Four rules protect you:

  1. No genuine government post is ever sold. Nobody - agent, "officer", consultancy - can arrange selection for money. The only payment in real recruitment is the application fee, paid on the official portal, typically a few hundred rupees.
  2. Verify the notification on the official domain. Every real notice lives on a .gov.in, .nic.in or official PSU domain. Every row in our list links to the post page where the official notification PDF and apply link are attached - if an offer you received isn't traceable to an official notice, treat it as fraud.
  3. No recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram DMs. Forwarded "joining letters" and interview calls demanding a deposit are scams, full stop.
  4. Cross-check suspicious notices against PIB Fact Check before sharing or paying anything.

How to Apply for Government Jobs Without Exam

  1. Open the post from the live list and read the official notification PDF - eligibility, age limits and fee are final there, not in any summary.
  2. Confirm you match the qualification and category requirements before paying any fee.
  3. Apply on the official portal linked in the notification; keep the registration number and fee receipt.
  4. For merit-list posts (GDS, apprentice), enter marks exactly as on your certificates - mismatches reject applications at verification.
  5. Track the post page for merit list / shortlist updates, or subscribe to WhatsApp/Telegram alerts so deadlines and results reach you automatically.

Government Jobs Without Exam - FAQs

1. Are there really government jobs without an exam?

Yes. Apprenticeship intakes, India Post GDS, sports and cultural quota posts, walk-in interviews and direct recruitment for experienced candidates are all filled without a written competitive exam. The live list at the top of this page shows every such notification currently open.

2. Which government jobs have no exam and no interview at all?

India Post GDS and Railway/PSU Act Apprentice selections use only a merit list of academic marks - there is no written test and no interview. Everything depends on your Class 10 (and ITI/diploma, where applicable) percentage.

3. What no-exam options exist for freshers after 10th, 12th or ITI?

Apprenticeships, GDS and trainee posts are the main fresher routes. Selection is a merit list prepared from academic marks, which is why these notifications attract very high application volumes despite no exam.

4. Can experienced professionals get a government job without an exam?

Yes. PSUs and autonomous bodies fill officer, manager and specialist posts by shortlisting candidates on qualification and experience, followed by a personal interview - no written test.

5. Are government jobs without exam permanent?

Often not. Apprenticeships are roughly one-year training engagements with a stipend, and many walk-in posts are contractual with fixed tenure. Direct-recruitment posts can be regular - the notification states the nature of each post, so check before applying.

6. Are there bank jobs without an exam?

A few. Some banks fill specialist and local officer posts through shortlisting plus interview. Bank apprenticeship drives vary - some are merit-based while others include an online test - so read each notification's selection clause.

7. Are there railway jobs without an exam?

Yes: Act Apprentice intakes (merit list), sports quota, cultural quota and Scouts & Guides quota. Apprentice intakes are large; the quota routes are small zonal recruitments with their own assessment process.

8. Is India Post GDS really without an exam?

Yes - selection is an online merit list generated from Class 10 marks, with no exam and no interview. Because of that, GDS is heavily targeted by paid-selection scams; apply only through the official GDS portal.

9. How do I identify fake "no exam" job offers?

No genuine government post is sold, fees are paid only on official portals, and no recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram messages. Verify every offer against the official notification on a government or PSU domain - if it isn't there, it's fraud.

10. How often is this list updated?

Daily. New notifications are added as they release, and every listing is removed automatically after its last date, so the list only ever shows posts you can still apply for.

Applications must be sent by post to the Regional Office, Delhi.

Vacancy Breakdown: 118 Posts Across 22 Specialties

The 118 Professor vacancies span clinical and pre-clinical disciplines. Reserved categories include backlog vacancies of 11 for SC, 6 for ST, and 23 for OBC. Eight posts are additionally reserved for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD).

Eligibility Criteria for ESIC Professor 2026

Understanding who qualifies is essential before applying. The eligibility conditions differ slightly for medical and non-medical candidates, and both must meet specific experience thresholds recognized by the National Medical Commission (NMC).

Age Limit

  • Maximum age: 50 years as on the closing date (27 July 2026)
  • SC/ST candidates: 5 years relaxation (upper limit: 55 years)
  • OBC candidates: 3 years relaxation (upper limit: 53 years)
  • PwBD candidates: 10 years relaxation (upper limit: 60 years; SC/ST PwBD: 15 years, OBC PwBD: 13 years) - subject to a maximum of 56 years
  • ESIC/Government employees: 5 years relaxation
  • Ex-Servicemen: 5 years relaxation, subject to minimum 6 months service after attestation

Educational Qualifications

For Medical Candidates (Essential):

  1. A recognized medical qualification included in the First or Second Schedule or Part-II of the Third Schedule to the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956.
  2. A postgraduate qualification - MD (Doctor of Medicine) or MS (Master of Surgery) or a recognized equivalent in the respective subject or allied discipline.

For Non-Medical Candidates (Essential):

  1. A Master's Degree in the concerned subject or allied discipline.
  2. A Doctorate degree from a recognized university in the respective subject or allied discipline.

Teaching Experience

Candidates must fulfill one of the following:

Option A: Four years of teaching experience as a Reader or Associate Professor in a recognized medical college in the concerned specialty.

Option B: Three years of teaching experience as an Associate Professor in a recognized medical college, plus a minimum of four research publications in indexed or national journals - published as the First Author in journals of National Associations or Societies of the respective specialties. Of these, at least two publications must have been during the tenure as Associate Professor.

Mode of Payment: A Demand Draft or Banker's Cheque of ₹500 drawn in favour of 'ESI Fund Account No. 2', payable at Delhi, on any scheduled bank. The DD/BC must be valid for at least three months and must be issued after the advertisement date (19 May 2026). Fee once paid is non-refundable.

ESIC Professor Recruitment 2026 - Pay Scale and Benefits

The Professor post carries Pay Level-13 in the Central Government Pay Matrix, with a pay range of ₹1,23,100 to ₹2,15,900 per month. In addition to basic pay, selected candidates are entitled to:

  • Dearness Allowance (DA)
  • Non-Practising Allowance (NPA) - as admissible to analogous posts in the Central Health Service
  • House Rent Allowance (HRA)
  • Transport Allowance

Promotional avenues are available under the Dynamic Assured Career Progression (DACP) guidelines of the Government of India.

ESIC Professor Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

The selection for ESIC Professor 2026 is based entirely on an interview conducted by a Selection Board. There is no written examination. Candidates who have applied will be assessed on experience and merit before being called.

Step-by-Step Selection Process

  1. Application Submission - Send the completed application form by Speed Post to reach ESIC Regional Office, Delhi by 27 July 2026.
  2. Shortlisting - If the number of applications is large, ESIC will shortlist candidates based on teaching experience at Associate Professor/Reader level or higher, beyond the minimum eligibility. Shortlisting is based solely on information and certificates submitted with the application - no subsequent documents will be accepted.
  3. Interview - Shortlisted candidates appear before the Selection Board at a venue decided by ESIC.
  4. Minimum Qualifying Marks in Interview (out of 100):
    • UR / EWS: 50 marks
    • OBC: 45 marks
    • SC / ST / PwBD: 40 marks
  5. Tie-Breaking (if scores are equal):
    • First: Elder candidate preferred.
    • Second: Candidate who passed the essential postgraduate degree earlier.
    • Third: Candidate who completed internship earlier.
  6. Reserve List - ESIC may draw a Reserve List as per UPSC guidelines.
  7. Probation - Selected candidates will be appointed on probation as per rules.

ESIC Professor Recruitment 2026 - How to Apply Step-by-Step

Candidates cannot apply online for this recruitment. The application is purely offline via Speed Post.

  1. Download the application form from the official ESIC notification (available at www.esic.gov.in).
  2. Fill in the application form completely in block letters. Ensure at least 10 state preferences for posting are listed.
  3. Attach a recent self-attested passport-size photograph firmly (not stapled) on the application form.
  4. Prepare a Demand Draft/Banker's Cheque of ₹500 (where applicable) in favour of 'ESI Fund Account No. 2', payable at Delhi. Write your name and address on the reverse side.
  5. Attach self-attested copies of all required documents (see Documents Required section below).
  6. Place the DD/BC pinned or clipped (not stapled or tagged) at the top of the application.
  7. Superscribe the envelope: "Application for the post of Professor for Medical Institutions"
  8. Send by Speed Post to: Regional Office Delhi, ESI Corporation DDA Complex Cum Office, 3rd & 4th Floor,, Rajendra Bhawan, Rajendra Place,, New Delhi - 110008
  9. Ensure delivery by 27 July 2026. ESIC will not be responsible for postal delays.

Documents Required with Application

Every applicant must submit self-attested copies of the following documents. Incomplete applications are liable to be summarily rejected without communication.

  • Demand Draft / Banker's Cheque (original, pinned at top)
  • Passport-size photograph (recent, firmly pasted)
  • Date of Birth proof - Matriculation/10th certificate or mark sheet (School Leaving Certificate accepted for Tamil Nadu and Kerala candidates only)
  • Degree certificates and mark sheets for all academic years (or provisional certificate with mark sheets)
  • Experience certificates from each employer, clearly stating duration, nature of work, and basic/consolidated pay
  • Research publication certificates/testimonials
  • Caste/Category certificate (SC/ST/OBC/EWS) in the prescribed central government format
  • OBC Non-Creamy Layer declaration (Annexure-II)
  • Certificate of Disability (PwBD candidates) in the prescribed format - minimum 40% disability
  • Ex-Servicemen certificate in prescribed proforma (if applicable)
  • Declaration that current employer has been informed (for serving government/ESIC employees)
  • Name-change supporting documents (if applicable - marriage certificate, divorce decree, or Deed Poll/Affidavit as appropriate)

ESIC Professor Recruitment 2026 - Posting Locations

Selected candidates are liable to be posted anywhere in India. ESIC operates medical colleges and PGIMSRs across the following states, and applicants must indicate at least 10 state preferences in the application form:

Rajasthan, Bihar, Karnataka, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Haryana, Telangana, Delhi, Maharashtra, Assam, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Jharkhand, and Gujarat.

Preference will be considered subject to administrative requirements and cannot be claimed as a matter of right.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

These pitfalls are frequently responsible for application rejections - check each before dispatch:

  1. Not attaching the DD/BC - Applications without the prescribed fee from paying categories are summarily rejected with no appeal.
  2. Submitting multiple applications under different categories - All such applications will be rejected outright.
  3. Requesting to add experience after submission - Only experience with certificates submitted with the original application is considered for shortlisting.
  4. Using the wrong DD format - Online transfers, UPI, or cheques other than DD/Banker's Cheque are not accepted.
  5. Not superscribing the envelope - Failure to write the prescribed text on the cover may result in the application being overlooked.
  6. Unsigned application form - Unsigned or incomplete forms are liable to rejection without notice.
  7. Sending experience certificates without duration/pay details - Certificates must clearly state start date, end date, nature of duties, and pay. Vague letters will not be counted.
  8. Listing fewer than 10 state preferences - The notification specifically advises candidates to fill at least 10 options.
  9. Tampered or altered documents - Any forgery or alteration will lead to cancellation and potential legal action.
  10. Relying on postal speed alone - Send applications well in advance; postal delays are the applicant's responsibility.

📄 Complete Details & Notification

The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) has released Advertisement No. 06/2026 inviting Online Recruitment Applications for 538 posts across more than 30 central government ministries and departments. Posts span disciplines including civil aviation, defence, forensic science, agriculture, mines, law, and education. Applications must be submitted through the UPSC ORA portal at https://upsconline.nic.in/ora/.

UPSC Recruitment 2026 - Age Relaxation

The standard age relaxations applicable to these posts are as follows. SC candidates receive 5 additional years, OBC candidates receive 3 additional years, and all PwBD candidates receive 10 additional years over and above their category relaxation. For certain posts with a base upper limit of 50 years, the PwBD maximum is capped at 56 years - this applies to the Regional Director (NCONF), Professor Sugar Engineering (NSI), Principal (A&N), and Consultant Ophthalmologist (UT Ladakh). UPSC may relax qualifications and experience at its discretion in writing for candidates otherwise well qualified.

Grade Point to Percentage Conversion (CME Pune and UT Ladakh posts)

Where a grade point system is in use and no conversion formula has been notified by the institution, the following equivalences apply as stated in the notification:

For UT Ladakh Lecturer and Engineering posts, ST candidates receive a 5% relaxation at Bachelor's and Master's level, making 55% (or equivalent grade) the minimum eligibility.

Special Condition - UT Ladakh Posts (Posts 60-70)

All posts under the Administration of the Union Territory of Ladakh are exclusively open to Domiciles of UT Ladakh. A valid Domicile Certificate issued by the Tehsildar under the Ladakh Civil Services Decentralization and Recruitment Rules, 2025 (published in the Gazette of India on 03.06.2025) is mandatory. Two eligible categories exist: Category A (holders of or eligible for Ladakh Resident Certificate) and Category B (children of LRC holders or those eligible). Reservation is governed by the Jammu and Kashmir Reservation Act, 2004, as extended to UT Ladakh and amended by the Ladakh Reservation (Amendment) Regulation, 2025 (No. 1 of 2025), and further by the Ladakh Reservation (Amendment) Rules, 2025 notified vide S.O. 77 dated 27.06.2025.

Troubleshooting and Common Mistakes

Candidates applying through the UPSC ORA portal can avoid common problems by following these general practices. Photograph and signature files must meet the portal's specified size and dimension requirements; uploading files that are too large or in an unsupported format is among the most frequent causes of incomplete applications. If a payment transaction fails, wait for the system to confirm the failure before attempting to pay again - making duplicate payments can cause complications that require manual resolution. Use an updated, stable browser on a desktop or laptop for the best experience; mobile browsers sometimes fail to render form fields correctly. Save your registration number and password immediately after registering, as the portal requires them for every subsequent login. Do not attempt to submit your application on the final day of the application window, as heavy traffic on the server is common and can cause timeouts or session errors.

SSC SSA/UDC Limited Departmental Competitive Examination 2025 - Selection Process & Exam Pattern

The examination consists of two parts: Part-I (Computer Based & Written Examination, 300 marks) and Part-II (Evaluation of Record of Service/APARs, 100 marks). Total marks = 400. Final selection will be made on the basis of aggregate performance in all parts. This is a competitive and not a qualifying examination.

Part-I: Computer Based & Written Examination (300 Marks)

Subject Paper No. No. of Questions Maximum Marks Time Duration Mode
General Awareness Paper-I 100 200 2 hours (2 hours 40 minutes for candidates eligible for Scribe) Computer Based Examination (Objective Type Multiple Choice)
English Language and Comprehension 100
Noting, Drafting & Office Procedure Paper-II -- 100 2 hours (2 hours 40 minutes for candidates eligible for Scribe) Written Examination (Descriptive / Conventional type)

Note: There will be negative marking of 0.25 marks for each wrong answer in Computer Based Examination (Paper-I). Candidates have to attempt the examination in the language (English/Hindi) as opted in the online Application Form. There will be no Question Paper in Braille for Visually Handicapped candidates.

Part-II: Evaluation of Record of Service (100 Marks)

Marks 100 marks earmarked for evaluation of record of service (APARs - Annual Performance Assessment Reports)
Usage Marks obtained in Part-II will be added for ascertaining the rank of the candidate. Once the APARs have been evaluated, no request for change in APAR grading will be entertained by the Commission under any circumstances.

Syllabus of the Examination

Paper Subject Syllabus / Topics
Paper-I (CBE) General Awareness Questions aimed at testing General Awareness of the environment around and its application to society. Current events; matters of everyday observations and experience in their scientific aspect; History, Culture, Geography, Economics, Science, General Politics and Scientific research relating to India and neighboring countries.
Paper-I (CBE) English Language and Comprehension Understanding and knowledge of English language: Vocabulary, spelling, grammar, sentence structure, synonyms, antonyms, sentence completion, phrases and idiomatic use of words, comprehension of a passage. Questions will be of matriculation level.
Paper-II (Written/Descriptive) Noting, Drafting & Office Procedure Knowledge of office procedure in the Secretariat and Attached Offices; ability to write and understand notes and drafts. Candidates are required to study the Manual of Office Procedure (including Ministry of Railways version), the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, Hand Book of orders issued by Ministry of Home Affairs regarding use of Hindi for official purpose of the Union, and Reservation Policy for SC/STs in services and orders issued by Government thereon from time to time.

Mode of Selection

Step 1 Based on performance in Paper-I (CBE) of Part-I, candidates will be shortlisted for evaluation of Paper-II (Descriptive Paper) of Part-I. Candidates not qualifying Paper-I will not be evaluated for Paper-II and will not be considered for further selection.
Step 2 Based on aggregate performance in Paper-I and Paper-II of Part-I, candidates will be shortlisted for evaluation of record of service (Part-II). Candidates not qualifying Part-I aggregate will not be eligible for Part-II evaluation.
Step 3 Final selection will be made on the basis of aggregate performance of candidates in Paper-I (CBE) + Paper-II (Descriptive) of Part-I and Part-II (APAR Evaluation). The Commission may fix minimum qualifying marks individually for Paper-I and Paper-II of Part-I.

Tie-Breaking Rules

1st Tie-Break Marks obtained in Paper-II (Descriptive)
2nd Tie-Break Marks obtained in part (b) of Paper-I (English Language and Comprehension)
3rd Tie-Break Date of birth - older candidates placed higher
4th Tie-Break Alphabetical order in which the names of the candidates appear

SSC JSA / LDC LDCE 2025 - Important Dates

Apply well before the deadline. SSC will not be responsible for failure to submit on account of heavy website load in the closing days, and no application received after the last date and time will be entertained under any circumstances.

Event Date
Notification Released 05-06-2026
Online Application Begins 05-06-2026
Last Date & Time to Apply Online 26-06-2026 (11:00 PM)
Forwarded Hard Copy to Reach SSC-NR 03-07-2026 (6:00 PM)

Computer Based Examination July – August 2026 (Tentative)
