SSC JSA / LDC LDCE 2025 - Eligibility Criteria

Educational Qualification

Candidates must have passed the 12th standard (Higher Secondary) examination from a recognised Board or equivalent. For the Railway Board Secretariat Clerical Service, candidates are additionally required to pass a typing test (35 w.p.m. in English or 30 w.p.m. in Hindi on computer) within one year of appointment.

Length of Service

A minimum of three years of regular service as a Group 'C' employee / MTS in Level-1 (Grade Pay ₹1,800) in the respective cadre, counted as on the crucial date applicable to that cadre.

Crucial Date (Varies by Cadre)

The crucial date for counting approved service and age is not the same for every department. Check yours carefully:

Crucial Date Applicable Cadres
01-07-2025 Central Passport Organisation, MEA (Cadre Cell), Bureau of Police Research & Development
01-08-2025 Railway Board Secretariat Clerical Service
01-01-2025 Central Administrative Tribunal, O/o Registrar General of India, NTRO, Dept. of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, O/o Development Commissioner (MSME), Central Translation Bureau, Official Language Wing

Age Limit & Relaxation

For most participating cadres, the maximum age is 45 years (50 years for SC/ST) as on the crucial date. Candidates should confirm the exact age condition for their own cadre from the notification. Permissible relaxation beyond the upper age limit:

Category Age Relaxation
SC / ST 5 years
Defence personnel disabled in operations 3 years
Defence personnel disabled in operations (SC/ST) 8 years

SSC JSA / LDC LDCE 2025 - Application Fee

For this Limited Departmental Competitive Examination, the notice does not prescribe an application fee for submitting the form. (A separate, non-refundable charge of ₹50 per question applies only if a candidate later chooses to challenge the tentative answer key - this is unrelated to the application itself.)

How to Apply for SSC JSA / LDC LDCE 2025

The process has two parts - One Time Registration (OTR) followed by the application - plus a mandatory offline forwarding step. Follow these steps:

  1. Generate OTR on the new website. Visit ssc.gov.in and click "Register Now." Any OTR created on the old site (ssc.nic.in) will not work on the new portal.
  2. Opt for Aadhaar-Based Authentication during OTR (recommended). Candidates who skip Aadhaar must upload the prescribed proof documents.
  3. Log in with your Registration Number and password, then open the JSA/LDC LDCE 2025 link under the "Live Exam" tab and click Apply.
  4. Fill the application - service details, cadre, crucial date, length of service, and age-relaxation code (if any). Information auto-filled from OTR is non-editable; use "Modify Registration" if a correction is needed.
  5. Capture your live photograph and upload your signature as per the specifications (see below).
  6. Upload the required documents (listed below) and Submit. Take a printout of the submitted application.
  7. Forward the hard copy through proper channel. Your Head of Department / Head of Office must forward the printed application along with service documents to: The Regional Director, Staff Selection Commission (Northern Region), Block No. 12, CGO Complex, Lodhi Road, New Delhi – 110003, so as to reach by 03-07-2026 (6:00 PM) - or 10-07-2026 for candidates abroad/A&N/Lakshadweep.

Critical: Only applications forwarded by the Head of Department/Office will be admitted. A correctly submitted online form alone is not enough.

Documents to Keep Ready Before You Start

  • Certified true copy of the first page of your Service Book (attested by HoD/HoO)
  • Certified particulars of service (posts held, scale of pay, nature of appointment)
  • Class 12th certificate / educational qualification proof (if applicable)
  • Caste/Category certificate (SC/ST), if claiming reservation
  • Disability certificate (Annexure-VII / VIII) for PwBD candidates
  • A recent passport-size photo for the live capture reference, and a scanned signature

Photograph & Signature Specifications

  • Photograph: Captured live via webcam/phone, in a well-lit area with a plain background. No cap, mask, or spectacles. Face must fill the on-screen red rectangle. Pre-existing/scanned photos are rejected.
  • Signature: JPEG/JPG, 10–20 KB, dimensions about 6.0 cm × 2.0 cm. Sign so the signature fills at least 80% of the box. Blurred or miniature signatures are rejected.

SSC JSA / LDC LDCE 2025 - Exam Pattern & Scheme

The examination carries 260 marks in total - 200 for Part-I (the exams) and 60 for Part-II (service record). Note that Paper-I is descriptive (written) and Paper-II is the objective Computer Based Test (CBT).

Part-I: Written + Computer Based Examination (200 Marks)

Paper Type Section Questions Max Marks Duration
Paper-I Descriptive (Written) Short Essay – 100 1 hr 30 min*
Paper-II Objective (CBT) (a) Language - General English or Samanya Hindi 50 50 2 hrs*
Paper-II Objective (CBT) (b) General Knowledge 50 50 (combined)

*Scribe-eligible candidates get 2 hours for Paper-I and 2 hours 40 minutes for Paper-II, plus 20 minutes compensatory time per hour.

  • Negative marking of 0.25 marks per wrong answer applies to Paper-II (CBT) only. There is no negative marking in the descriptive Paper-I.
  • Candidates must attempt the exam in the language (English/Hindi) chosen in the application form.

Part-II: Evaluation of Record of Service (60 Marks)

60 marks are reserved for evaluation of the APARs (Annual Performance Appraisal Reports). These marks are added to determine the final rank. Once evaluated, no request to change APAR grading is entertained.

SSC JSA / LDC LDCE 2025 - Selection Process

This is a competitive, not qualifying examination. Selection proceeds stage by stage:

  1. Paper-II (CBT) qualifying: Candidates must clear the minimum marks fixed for Paper-II to have their Paper-I evaluated.
  2. Paper-I (Descriptive) evaluation: Only those qualifying in Paper-II have their descriptive paper assessed.
  3. APAR evaluation (Part-II): Based on the aggregate of Paper-I + Paper-II, shortlisted candidates move to service-record evaluation.
  4. Final merit: Prepared on the combined total of Paper-I + Paper-II + Part-II (APAR) = 260 marks, cadre-wise, subject to reservation. Ties are resolved by Paper-I marks, then Paper-II part (a), then Paper-II total, then date of birth (older ranked higher), then alphabetical order.

SSC JSA / LDC LDCE 2025 - Syllabus

  • Paper-I (Short Essay): One essay of 400–500 words on any of the specified subjects.
  • Paper-II (a) Language: Simple composition and applied grammar (in the chosen English/Hindi medium).
  • Paper-II (b) General Knowledge: Current events, matters of everyday observation and experience, and general information about India.

SSC JSA / LDC Salary 2026

Selected candidates are appointed in Pay Level-2 (₹19,900 – ₹63,200 per month) under the 7th CPC, as Group 'C' Non-Gazetted staff. In addition to basic pay, employees are entitled to Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA), Transport Allowance, and other benefits as admissible under Central Government rules for the respective department.

Common Reasons SSC Applications Get Rejected

A large share of LDCE applications fail on avoidable mistakes. Double-check all of these before submitting:

  • Application not forwarded by the Head of Department/Office (the single biggest cause of rejection).
  • Multiple applications submitted for the same exam.
  • Photograph with a cap/spectacles, dark background, blurred, or a pre-existing (scanned) photo instead of a live capture.
  • Signature that is blurred, miniature, or below the size norm.
  • Wrong OTR details - name, father's/mother's name, or date of birth not matching the matriculation certificate (OTR data is non-editable).
  • Hard copy reaching SSC-NR after the deadline, or incomplete documents.

What to Do If the SSC Website Is Slow

Traffic on the SSC portal spikes near the closing date. If you face issues:

  • Apply during off-peak hours - late at night or early morning - rather than on the last day.
  • Clear your browser cache/cookies, or use an incognito/private tab.
  • Try a different browser (Chrome, Firefox, Edge) or switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data.
  • Keep all documents pre-scanned and ready in the correct format so a session timeout doesn't cost you the whole form.
  • Save a draft frequently and take a printout immediately after final submission.

Exam Day Guidelines

  • The exam is conducted in Delhi-NCR only; there is no centre abroad. A candidate posted abroad must appear in India at their own expense.
  • The Admission Certificate is issued online via sscnr.nic.in (3–4 days before the exam); it is never sent by post.
  • Carry your original Departmental Identity Card along with a hard copy of the Admission Certificate.
  • Candidates not Aadhaar-authenticated during OTR must report early with two passport-size photographs and an original photo ID showing date of birth.
  • No Travelling Allowance is paid by SSC.
  • Mobile phones, Bluetooth/wireless devices, smartwatches, and electronic gadgets are strictly prohibited. SSC conducts post-exam log, biometric, and CCTV analysis, and malpractice attracts debarment of 1 to 7 years depending on the offence.

  • Help Desk (SSC-HQ): 1800-309-3063 (Toll-free)
  • SSC (Northern Region): 011-24363343
  • Official Websites: ssc.gov.in (HQ) · sscnr.nic.in (Northern Region)

What Is the RBI Young Professional Programme?

The RBI Young Professional programme is a unique initiative by the Reserve Bank of India designed to bring domain specialists into the central bank's functioning on a contractual basis. Unlike recruitment for regular officer grades, this programme targets individuals with specialized postgraduate or technical expertise who can contribute meaningfully to short-to-medium-term policy-related research and analytical assignments.

Selected Young Professionals work within RBI's Central Office Departments in Mumbai, gaining direct exposure to India's most consequential financial, monetary, and regulatory policy decisions. The engagement enriches both the Bank's analytical capacity and the professional development of selected candidates. It is not a pathway to permanent employment at RBI, but it is widely regarded as an extraordinary professional experience within India's financial policy ecosystem.

  • Essential Qualification: Postgraduate degree or equivalent in Cyber Security / Information Security / Computer Science / IT / Data Science / AI or a related field.
  • Desirable Qualifications & Certifications: CISSP, CISM, CEH, ISO 27001 Lead Auditor, AWS/Azure Security; published research in IT, Cybersecurity, or Public Policy journals.

RBI Young Professional Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must satisfy the following baseline conditions to be considered for any of the 12 Young Professional positions at RBI. These are non-negotiable and checked at the time of document verification.

  • Nationality: Must be an Indian citizen.
  • Age Limit: Must be above 21 years and not more than 30 years of age as on July 6, 2026. The notification does not mention any age relaxation for reserved categories under this recruitment.
  • Educational Qualification: Must meet the post-specific eligibility criteria as detailed in Annexure-III of the official notification. All qualifications must be from a recognized institution in India or abroad. In cases of similar or alternative qualifications, RBI retains sole authority to determine equivalency.
  • Agreement to Terms: Candidates must agree to the Terms and Conditions of Engagement as specified in the notification.
  • Application Mode: Must apply via email in the prescribed proforma (Annexure-VI of the official notification).

Each post has its own essential qualification. Meeting the general age criterion alone does not guarantee eligibility - always check the post-specific educational requirement before applying.

Monthly Stipend and Terms of Engagement

Understanding what this role offers - and what it does not - is essential before applying. RBI's YP engagement is a contractual position with a generous stipend but with clearly defined boundaries.

Remuneration

A fixed monthly stipend of ₹1,50,000 will be paid throughout the engagement period, subject to applicable tax deductions. No additional allowances, HRA, or benefits are provided over and above this stipend.

Contract Duration

The initial contract tenure is 3 years, which may be extended by mutual agreement for a total period not exceeding 5 years. The extension decision is based solely on the Bank's assessment of the YP's performance and is at RBI's discretion.

Nature of Engagement

This is a contractual, full-time engagement - not a regular or permanent appointment. The YP will have no claim to any regular or permanent position at RBI by virtue of this engagement. There is no employer-employee relationship between RBI and the YP.

Leave Policy

YPs are entitled to 15 days of leave per calendar year, accrued on a pro-rata basis from the date of joining. Leave cannot be carried forward to the next year. Absence beyond this entitlement is treated as leave without pay, with a proportionate deduction from the monthly stipend. Unauthorized absence for 8 or more consecutive working days without valid reason may lead to contract termination.

Termination and Notice Period

Either party may terminate the contract with 3 months' notice. However, during the first 6 months of the initial tenure, the contract may be terminated by either side without any notice period.

Other Conditions

  • Place of engagement is Mumbai; no residential accommodation will be provided by RBI
  • No part-time work for any private or public body is permitted during the engagement without prior written permission from RBI
  • YPs must produce a medical fitness certificate and a satisfactory police verification report on selection
  • A code of conduct agreement and secrecy undertaking must be signed on joining
  • In the event of death, injury, or illness during tenure, neither the YP nor their dependents are entitled to compensation or employment from RBI

RBI Young Professional Recruitment 2026 Apply Link & Process

The application process for RBI YP 2026 is entirely email-based. There is no online portal, no registration system, and no walk-in interview. Every step must be followed precisely to avoid rejection.

Step 1 - Download the Application Proforma: Download Annexure-VI from the official notification document available at www.rbi.org.in. Fill it out completely. Fields marked with asterisk (*) are mandatory.

Step 2 - Prepare Your Documents: Compile all the following in PDF format:

  • Duly filled application proforma (Annexure-VI) with recent colour photograph (3.5 x 4.5 cm) pasted
  • Curriculum Vitae (CV)
  • Degree certificates for essential and desirable qualifications (provisional certificate acceptable if the degree is pending)
  • Statement of Interest (explaining why you are applying for the specific post)
  • A sample of academic or policy writing
  • A reference/recommendation letter from a professional referee (preferably from your current/previous employer or academic institution)

Step 3 - Check the Email Specifications:

  • All documents must be in PDF format only - other formats may be blocked by RBI's security filters
  • Total attachment size must not exceed 5 MB
  • The email body must be concise (one or two lines) and unconditional - no additional statements

Step 4 - Format the Email Subject Line Correctly:
The subject line must follow this exact format: "YP Application - [Post Code] - [Your Full Name]"
Example: YP Application - YP0626FIN01 - Ramesh Kumar

Step 5 - Send the Application:
Email your complete application to [email protected] before the deadline.

Step 6 - Applying for Multiple Posts:
If you wish to apply for more than one position, send a separate email for each post. Each email must include a complete, independent set of all required documents.

  • [Apply Online] - Send your application email to [email protected]
  • [PDF Download Link] - Download the official notification and Annexure-VI application proforma from www.rbi.org.in

Last Date: July 6, 2026

Selection Process for RBI YP 2026

Submitting a complete and eligible application is only the first step. The selection process for RBI Young Professionals involves multiple stages, and meeting the minimum eligibility is not a guarantee of progression.

Stage 1 - Preliminary Screening: A screening committee reviews all received applications against the eligibility criteria and the quality of supporting documents. The Bank reserves the right to limit the number of candidates called for interview.

Stage 2 - Document Verification: Shortlisted candidates will be required to submit and verify original documents related to age, educational qualifications, and experience.

Stage 3 - Interview: Shortlisted candidates will receive an interview call letter via email only. No physical call letters will be sent by post. Candidates must make their own travel and accommodation arrangements for the interview.

Reserve List: RBI maintains a reserve list of suitable candidates, valid for one year from the date of publication of the selection list.

RBI's decision regarding shortlisting, interview, and all aspects of engagement is final. No correspondence will be entertained in this regard.

Candidates wondering how marks are normalized can note that the Bank combines scores from both stages using this 70:30 ratio before preparing the final merit list, circle-wise and category-wise.

  1. Online Written Test – Tentatively scheduled for August 2026 across multiple centres nationwide; call letters will be issued via the Bank's website, SMS, and email.
  2. Shortlisting – Based on Professional Knowledge cut-off marks, plus minimum qualifying marks in General Aptitude sections.
  3. Interview – Carries 100 marks; conducted for a category-wise adequate number of shortlisted candidates.
  4. Local Language Proficiency Test (LLPT) – Conducted for provisionally selected candidates before joining; candidates with 10th/12th mark sheets showing the relevant local language as a subject are exempted.
  5. Final Result & Wait List – A circle-wise and category-wise wait list valid for one year (or until a fresh advertisement, whichever is earlier) is maintained for non-joining or termination cases.

All applications must be submitted exclusively through the EPI official website. Applications sent by email or post will not be accepted. Follow each step carefully - no modifications are allowed after final submission.

Shortlisting & Selection Process

EPI uses a merit-based shortlisting process to filter applicants before calling them for interview. Understanding this process helps you assess your competitive standing before applying.

  • Candidates are shortlisted based on percentage of marks in the required qualification and post-qualification experience.
  • Fraction of percentage is ignored - 54.9% is treated as less than 55% and will lead to rejection.
  • If applications are high in volume, EPI may conduct a Written Test before the interview stage.
  • The shortlist will be published on the EPI website; selected candidates will also be informed by email.
  • The final list of selected candidates will be hosted on the EPI website after the interview.
  • Interview venue: Western Regional Office (WRO), Mumbai. No TA/DA is admissible for attending the interview.

CGPA to Percentage Conversion - EPI's Official Rules

If your degree certificate shows CGPA instead of percentage, EPI has specific conversion norms you must follow when filling your application form.

  • If the university provides a conversion formula: Use the university's own conversion and obtain a certificate from the university confirming the equivalent percentage. Submit this certificate at the time of interview.
  • If the university does not provide a conversion formula: A minimum CGPA of 6 on a 10-point scale will be treated as equivalent to 60%. For scales other than 10-point, the score will be prorated accordingly.

Selection Process - How Candidates Are Chosen

The IAF MTS recruitment follows a clearly defined selection process. Knowing each stage in advance helps candidates prepare effectively and avoid being eliminated at any step.

Stage 1 - Application Scrutiny

All applications received will be examined for age limit compliance, minimum educational qualification, required documents, and certificates. Only eligible candidates will be shortlisted for the written test.

Stage 2 - Written Test

Eligible shortlisted candidates will be called for a written test. The selection of candidates will be based purely on performance in the written test — no interview is conducted.

Written Test Syllabus covers four areas:

  • General Intelligence and Reasoning
  • Numerical Aptitude
  • General English
  • General Awareness

The question-cum-answer paper will be available in both English and Hindi.

Stage 3 - Document Verification

Shortlisted candidates after the written test must bring original certificates and copies of the annexure attached with the application at the time of document verification.

Important: Candidates are required to bring original certificates of SC/ST/OBC/EWS/PwBD/ESM, educational qualifications, technical qualifications, and experience at every stage of recruitment. ISRO ISTRAC Apprentices Recruitment 2026 - Eligibility Criteria

The ISRO ISTRAC Apprentice 2026 eligibility rules are strict and candidates should verify each condition carefully before applying. Only those who passed their qualifying examination as regular candidates are eligible - correspondence, private, or sandwich course degrees are not accepted. Candidates currently pursuing higher studies (e.g., B.E./B.Tech for diploma holders) are also not eligible.

Educational Qualification

  • Graduate Apprentice (GA01-GA06): B.E./B.Tech in the relevant engineering discipline from any recognised University. For GA07 (Library Science): MLISc. (Library and Information Science).
  • Diploma Apprentice (DA01-DA06): Diploma in Engineering awarded by a recognised State Board in the respective discipline. DA06 requires Diploma in Commercial Practice.
  • ITI Trade Apprentice (TA01-TA05): ITI certificate in the concerned trade from any recognised University.

Year of Passing Condition

Candidates must have passed their qualifying course in 2024, 2025, or 2026 only. Candidates are also required to join within 3 years of acquiring the degree/diploma/ITI (calculated from the month and year of passing as stated in the certificate). If this three-year window lapses before the date of joining, the candidature will be cancelled.

NATS Registration (Mandatory)

Every candidate must register on the National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS) portal at nats.education.gov.in before applying. The NATS Enrolment Number must be included in the email application. Applications without a valid NATS Enrolment Number are liable to be rejected. Candidates must upload their Degree/Diploma/ITI certificate and a valid government-issued ID on the NATS portal during registration.

Other Eligibility Conditions

  • Only Indian Nationals are eligible to apply.
  • Ex-apprentices, candidates currently undergoing apprenticeship elsewhere, or candidates with one year or more of work experience in Government/Public/Private Sector as on the date of joining are not eligible.
  • Combining this apprenticeship with any other institution's apprenticeship is not permitted.
  • Courses must be recognised by any University in India or State Boards.

Application Fee

ISRO ISTRAC has not prescribed any application fee for this apprenticeship recruitment. The application process is free of cost for all candidates across all categories.

How to Apply - Email Only

Applications for ISRO ISTRAC Apprentice 2026 are accepted exclusively via email - no online portal, no postal applications. Candidates must send their application to the dedicated email ID of the location they are applying for. If applying to multiple locations, separate emails must be sent to each location's dedicated email address.

Step-by-Step Application Process

  1. Register on the NATS portal at nats.education.gov.in and obtain your NATS Enrolment Number.
  2. Prepare scanned copies of: Final Degree/Diploma/ITI Certificate (or final year/semester mark sheet if certificate is awaited), Class X and Pre-University marks card/certificate, and NATS Enrolment Number.
  3. Compose an email to the correct location-specific email ID (see table below).
  4. In the Subject Line, mention the Post Code - e.g., "Application for Post Code: GA02".
  5. In the body of the email, clearly state: Name, Contact Number, Degree/Diploma/ITI Details, Year of Passing, and NATS Enrolment ID.
  6. Attach all required documents and send before 31 July 2026.

ISRO ISTRAC Apprentices Recruitment 2026- Selection Process

The ISRO ISTRAC Apprentice selection process consists of document scrutiny followed by an in-person interview. There is no written examination. Candidates shortlisted after screening will be called to the respective location for document verification and interview, and a merit panel will be drawn based on academic scores and interview performance.

  1. Application Scrutiny: Submitted emails are screened for eligibility and completeness.
  2. Shortlisting: Eligible candidates are shortlisted based on academic percentage and other criteria.
  3. Document Verification / Interview: Shortlisted candidates are called to the respective centre. Interviews are held at Lucknow (27-28 August 2026), Sri Vijaya Puram (03-04 September 2026), and Bengaluru (09-11 September 2026). Reporting time at all centres is 8:30 AM.
  4. Panel Formation: A merit panel is prepared based on Degree/Diploma/ITI academic scores and interview performance.
  5. Final Induction: Apprentices are inducted against vacant positions strictly based on their rank in the panel. Selected candidates are informed only via email.

Important: Candidates shortlisted for document verification/interview are not eligible for Travelling Allowance (TA). No request to change the place of interview or place of posting will be entertained.

Troubleshooting & Common Mistakes to Avoid

Many eligible candidates get rejected due to avoidable errors in the email application. Review these common pitfalls carefully before sending your application to ISRO ISTRAC.

  • Wrong email ID for location: Each training location has a separate email ID. Sending your Bengaluru application to the Lucknow email ID will result in rejection. Double-check the email address against the location you are targeting.
  • Missing Post Code in subject line: The subject line must clearly mention the Post Code (e.g., "Application for Post Code: GA02"). Emails without the Post Code may not be processed.
  • No NATS Enrolment Number: Registration on nats.education.gov.in is mandatory before applying. Not including the NATS Enrolment Number in the email body is grounds for rejection.
  • Passing year outside 2024-2026: If you passed your qualifying course before 2024, you are not eligible regardless of your marks or experience.
  • Applying with a private or sandwich course degree: Degrees obtained via private mode, correspondence, or sandwich courses are explicitly not accepted. Only regular candidates qualify.
  • Currently pursuing higher studies: Diploma holders currently doing B.E./B.Tech, or graduates currently doing M.E./M.Tech, are not eligible.
  • One year or more of work experience: Candidates with one year or more of work experience in Government, Public, or Private Sector as on the joining date are not eligible.
  • Applying to multiple locations in one email: Send separate emails to separate location-specific IDs. Do not combine locations in a single email.

Number of Attempts Allowed in SBI PO Exam

SBI has fixed a maximum number of attempts permissible for this exam based on category, and candidates who have already exhausted their permissible chances are not eligible to apply again. Appearing in the Main Examination counts as one attempt, while appearing only in the Preliminary Examination does not count as an attempt.

Category Maximum Permissible Chances
UR / EWS 6
UR (PwBD) / EWS (PwBD) / OBC / OBC (PwBD) 9
SC / SC (PwBD) / ST / ST (PwBD) No Restriction

SBI PO Application Fee 2026

The application fee for SBI PO Recruitment 2026 is Rs 750 for Unreserved (UR), EWS, and OBC candidates, while SC, ST, and PwBD candidates are exempted from paying any fee. This fee is non-refundable once paid and cannot be carried forward or held in reserve for any other examination, so candidates should confirm their category and details before making the payment.

CIBIL Score Requirement for SBI PO Candidates

A distinctive eligibility condition for this recruitment relates to credit history, since SBI PO is a banking role with financial responsibility. Candidates who have defaulted on repayment under any loan, NBFC, or financial institution arrangement, including credit card dues, and whose accounts reflect adverse credit history in CIBIL or another recognised credit agency, must regularise or repay all outstanding dues on or before the date of joining the Bank. If the adverse status has not been updated in CIBIL records by the joining date, candidates must either get the status updated or produce a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the lender confirming there are no outstanding dues; failure to do so will render the candidate ineligible and the offer of appointment will be withdrawn. Candidates are advised to check their CIBIL score before applying.

SBI PO Selection Process 2026: Prelims, Mains & Interview

Selection for SBI PO Recruitment 2026 follows a three-phase process: Phase-I Preliminary Examination, Phase-II Main Examination, and Phase-III Psychometric Test, Group Exercise & Interview. Candidates must clear each phase to be considered for the next, and only the marks from Phase-II and Phase-III are carried forward to prepare the final merit list.

Phase-I: SBI PO Prelims Exam Pattern 2026

The Preliminary Examination is an online objective test carrying 100 marks, to be completed in 1 hour, with separate timing for each of its three sections. There is no sectional cut-off in the Preliminary Exam, but a category-wise merit list is prepared based on the aggregate score, and candidates numbering approximately 10 times the vacancies in each category are shortlisted for the Main Exam.

Section No. of Questions Marks Duration
English Language 40 - 20 minutes
Quantitative Aptitude 30 - 20 minutes
Reasoning Ability 30 - 20 minutes
Total 100 100 1 hour

Phase-II: SBI PO Mains Exam Pattern 2026

The Main Examination is conducted online and consists of an Objective Test of 200 marks and a Descriptive Test of 30 marks, taken together in 3 hours 30 minutes. The descriptive paper is administered immediately after the objective test, and candidates must type their answers directly on the computer.

Section No. of Questions Max Marks Duration
Reasoning & Computer Aptitude 40 60 50 minutes
Data Analysis & Interpretation 30 60 45 minutes
General Awareness / Economy / Banking Knowledge 60 60 45 minutes
English Language 40 20 40 minutes
Objective Test Total 170 200 3 hours
Descriptive Test (Email / Situation Analysis / Report or Precis Writing) 3 30 30 minutes
Grand Total 230 3 hours 30 minutes  

Each candidate must score a minimum qualifying mark in every individual section, including the descriptive paper, with sectional cut-offs decided by the Bank based on vacancies. A category-wise merit list is then prepared from the aggregate Main Exam score, and candidates numbering approximately 3 times the category-wise vacancies are shortlisted for Phase-III.

There is also a penalty for wrong answers in both the Preliminary and Main objective tests: for every wrong answer, 1/4th of the marks assigned to that question is deducted, while unattempted questions carry no penalty.

Phase-III: Psychometric Test, Group Exercise & Interview

Shortlisted candidates undergo a Psychometric Test for personality profiling, followed by a Group Exercise (20 marks) and a Personal Interview (30 marks), totalling 50 marks. The Psychometric Test findings are shared with the interview panel to give a fuller perspective on each candidate, and all questions in this test are mandatory.

Final Merit List and Normalisation

The marks from Phase-II (Main Exam, both Objective and Descriptive) and Phase-III (Group Exercise & Interview) are normalised to 100 marks each before being combined into the final merit list; marks from the Preliminary Exam are not added at this stage.

Component Maximum Marks Normalised Marks
Main Examination (Objective + Descriptive) 230 75
Group Exercise & Interview 50 25
Total 280 100

If two or more candidates score identical marks at the cut-off point in the final merit list, they are ranked according to age in descending order, meaning the older candidate is placed higher.

SBI PO Apply Online 2026: Step-by-Step Registration Guide

Candidates can apply for SBI PO Recruitment 2026 only in online mode, from 18 June 2026 to 8 July 2026; no other mode of application is accepted. Before starting, candidates must have a valid personal email ID and mobile number kept active until the declaration of the final result, since all call letters and result-related communication will be sent there.

  1. Visit SBI's official careers portal at https://sbi.bank.in/web/careers/current-openings (also accessible at https://bank.sbi/web/careers/current-openings) and locate Advertisement No. CRPD/PO/2026-27/09.
  2. Download and carefully read the detailed advertisement PDF before proceeding with registration.
  3. Click Apply Online and open the registration form under "Current Openings."
  4. Keep scanned images ready in advance: your photograph (4.5cm x 3.5cm, 200×230 pixels, 20–50 KB), signature (140×60 pixels, 10–20 KB), left-hand thumb impression (3cm x 3cm, 240×240 pixels, 20–50 KB), and a hand-written declaration (10cm x 5cm, 800×400 pixels, 50–100 KB), all in JPG/JPEG format.
  5. Fill in the application form carefully; you can save a partially completed form, which generates a provisional registration number and password that you must note down to resume later.
  6. Capture a live photograph through your webcam or mobile phone during registration, as this is mandatory in addition to the uploaded photograph.
  7. Recheck every field for accuracy, since no edits are allowed once the form is finally submitted.
  8. Pay the applicable application fee online through Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, or UPI; SC, ST, and PwBD candidates are exempt from the fee.
  9. On successful payment, download and print the e-receipt and application form for your records.
  10. Complete your application well before 8 July 2026 to avoid last-minute technical issues caused by heavy website traffic.

You can also apply directly through the dedicated SBI PO registration link at https://ibpsreg.ibps.in/sbipojun26/.

SBI PO Salary 2026: Pay Scale and CTC

Selected candidates for SBI PO Recruitment 2026 will draw a starting basic pay of Rs 48,480, plus 4 advance increments, in the Junior Management Grade Scale-I (JMGS-I) pay scale of 48480-2000/7-62480-2340/2-67160-2680/7-85920. In addition to basic pay, officers are eligible for Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA), City Compensatory Allowance (CCA), Provident Fund, the National Pension System (NPS), Leave Fare Concession (LFC), medical facilities, lease rental facility, and other allowances as per the Bank's prevailing rules. The approximate CTC at the initial pay scale for the Mumbai Centre works out to Rs 21.97 Lacs.

In-Hand Salary Calculator 2026

Joining, Bond and Probation Period

Selected candidates must complete a basic banking knowledge online course before joining and will be designated as Probationary Officers, placed on probation for two years with continuous performance assessment. At the time of joining, candidates must execute a bond of Rs 2.00 Lacs, committing to serve the Bank for a minimum period of three years; this bond is invoked if the candidate resigns before completing three years of service. Officers who clear the probation assessment standards are confirmed in JMGS-I, and SBI's promotion policy offers a path for high-performing officers to reach senior and top management grades, including opportunities for international postings.

SBI PO Exam Preparation 2026: Strategy, Exam Pattern, Selection Process & Study Plan

Documents and Identity Proof Required at Examination

Candidates must carry specific documents at each stage of the selection process, and missing or mismatched documents can lead to disqualification. At the time of the Preliminary and Main Examinations, candidates must bring a valid photo identity proof such as a Passport, Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Driving Licence, Voter's ID Card, or Bank Passbook with an attested photograph, along with a self-attested photocopy. The notification also specifies that candidates must possess a valid Aadhaar card, as SBI conducts online Aadhaar verification at different stages of the selection process, and biometric verification (photo and thumb impression/IRIS scan) may also be carried out.

For the Main Exam specifically, candidates must bring the duly authenticated Original Preliminary Exam Call Letter along with the authenticated ID proof copy, the Main Exam Call Letter, and two additional photographs identical to the one used during registration; candidates without these will not be allowed to appear. Use of mobile phones or any electronic devices inside the examination or interview premises is strictly banned and can lead to disqualification.

Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying for SBI PO 2026

Many otherwise eligible candidates lose out due to small, avoidable errors during the application process, so it helps to be deliberate at each step. Keep your photograph, signature, thumb impression, and hand-written declaration within the exact pixel dimensions and file-size ranges specified, since uploads outside these limits will trigger an error and block submission; also remember that signatures and the hand-written declaration in capital letters are not accepted.

Avoid waiting until the closing date of 8 July 2026 to register, as heavy website traffic close to the deadline is a common cause of failed submissions, and SBI does not take responsibility for applications that fail to go through for this reason. Double-check your category selection before final submission, since no change of category is permitted at any stage after registration, and incorrectly chosen reserved or unreserved status cannot be corrected later. If an online payment fails or appears incomplete, register again and make the payment afresh rather than assuming the transaction went through, since the fee is strictly non-refundable. Finally, save your provisional registration number and password immediately after saving your form, and keep multiple copies of your registration photograph ready, as these are needed at every subsequent stage of the selection process.

How to Apply for Central Bank of India Apprentice Recruitment 2026

The application process involves two portals. Here is a step-by-step guide:

Step 1 - Register on NATS Portal Visit https://nats.education.gov.in and navigate to the "Student Register/Login" section. Complete your registration and note your Enrolment ID, which is required for all future correspondence.

Step 2 - Find CBI Apprenticeship on NATS After logging in, visit https://nats.education.gov.in/student_type.php to find and apply to the Central Bank of India apprenticeship advertisement.

Step 3 - Complete Application on BEEP Portal After applying on NATS, you will receive an email from BFSI SSC ([email protected]) with a link to register on https://beep.bfsissc.com. Complete your final application here by entering caste category, district preferences, and other details.

Step 4 - Pay the Application Fee Pay the applicable fee online through the BEEP portal. The application is complete only after successful payment.

Step 5 - Save Your Application Take a printout of the system-generated online application form after submitting. Do not make multiple submissions; only the last valid completed application will be retained.

Selection Process for Central Bank of India Apprentice Recruitment 2026

Selection involves multiple stages. Candidates must clear all stages to be engaged as apprentices.

Stage 1 - Online Written Examination

The exam is objective type, conducted by BFSI SSC. It will be taken from the candidate's own home on their own device - no admit card or examination centre is required.

Subject Questions Marks Duration
General / Financial Awareness 20 20 -
Quantitative & Reasoning Aptitude 20 20 -
Computer Knowledge 20 20 -
General English 20 20 -
Central Bank of India Products & Services 20 20 -
Total 100 100 60 minutes
  • Medium: English/Hindi (General English section in English only)
  • No negative marking for wrong answers
  • Tie-breaking rule: if two candidates score equally, the older candidate ranks higher (descending order of age)
  • Details on CBI Products & Services will be shared on the bank's official website in due course

Stage 2 - Test of Local Language

Candidates must be proficient (reading, writing, speaking, and understanding) in the specified official language of the state they apply for. This test is conducted after qualifying the online exam at a centre decided by the bank, at the candidate's own expense.

Candidates who have studied the specified local language at the 10th or 12th standard level (as evidenced by mark sheets) are exempt from the language test.

Stage 3 - Document Verification

Qualified candidates are called to the relevant CBI Regional/Zonal Office for verification of all original documents, including date of birth proof, graduation certificates, category certificates, and any other relevant documents.

Stage 4 - Medical Fitness Verification

Final engagement is subject to the candidate being declared medically fit by a qualified medical practitioner or MBBS doctor, as per the bank's requirements.

Stipend, Training Conditions, and Benefits

Understanding what to expect during the apprenticeship helps candidates plan ahead.

  • Monthly Stipend: ₹15,000 per month for the 12-month training period
  • No other allowances or employee benefits are provided
  • Leave: One casual leave per month; public/bank holidays as applicable; no other leave types
  • Working hours: Same as clerical staff of the bank; no overtime is permitted
  • No hostel, transport, or residential accommodation is provided by the bank
  • An assessment test may be conducted after completion, followed by certification as per prevailing guidelines
  • Apprentices are trainees, not employees - no labour laws or employee benefits apply
  • Apprentices cannot form or join any union

Contract of Apprenticeship

Candidates selected after document verification will receive a digital apprenticeship contract through the NATS government portal (https://nats.education.gov.in). They must accept the contract within the stipulated timeframe. No candidate can begin training without an approved apprenticeship contract.

Termination Conditions

The contract may be terminated in the following situations:

  • Non-reporting on the date of commencement of On-Job Training
  • Automatic termination on expiry of the 12-month training period
  • Mutual application to the Apprenticeship Advisor (BFSI SSC) before completion, with stated reasons
  • Misconduct by the apprentice, with written notice from the bank
  • If the Apprenticeship Advisor finds either party has failed to fulfil the contract terms

Documents Required at the Time of Document Verification

Candidates must carry originals plus self-attested photocopies of all the following:

  • System-generated printout of online application/NATS enrolment form
  • Date of Birth proof (Birth Certificate or Class X certificate with DOB)
  • Photo identity proof
  • Individual semester/year-wise mark sheets and final degree certificate
  • Caste certificate (for SC/ST/OBC/EWS candidates) in the Government of India prescribed format
  • OBC certificate must explicitly contain the non-creamy layer clause and be valid as on the date of the Language Test (issued within one year)
  • Disability certificate from District Medical Board (for PwBD candidates)
  • Income and Asset Certificate (for EWS candidates) issued by competent authority

Reservation for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD)

Under Section 34 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, reservation for PwBD is on a horizontal basis within the overall vacancies for each state. The qualifying disability categories include:

  • Visual Impairment (Blindness and Low Vision)
  • Hearing Impairment (Deaf and Hard of Hearing)
  • Orthopedic/Locomotor Disability (OA, OL, BL, OAL)
  • Cerebral Palsy, Leprosy Cured, Dwarfism, Acid Attack Victims, Muscular Dystrophy
  • Intellectual Disability (Autism Spectrum Disorder, Specific Learning Disability, Mental Illness)
  • Multiple Disabilities

A total of 45 seats each are reserved for VI, HI, OH, and ID categories, amounting to 180 PwBD seats across the country.

Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) Eligibility

Candidates not covered under SC/ST/OBC reservation and whose family gross annual income is below ₹8 lakh from all sources (salary, agriculture, business, profession) qualify for EWS reservation. Additionally, the family must not own:

  • 5 acres or more of agricultural land
  • A residential flat of 1,000 sq. ft. or more
  • A residential plot of 100 sq. yards or more in notified municipalities
  • A residential plot of 200 sq. yards or more outside notified municipalities

The EWS benefit requires an Income and Asset Certificate in the prescribed Government of India format, issued by a competent authority.

Where to Find Updates and Announcements

All announcements, addendums, and corrigenda will be published exclusively on:

  • Central Bank of India official website: Click here (Career section → Current Opportunities)
  • BFSI SSC portal: https://bfsissc.com
  • BEEP portal: https://beep.bfsissc.com (under "My Applied Opportunities")

Bank of Baroda Professionals Recruitment 2026 - Apply Online

Applications for this recruitment can be submitted only through the online mode on Bank of Baroda's official website - no offline or postal applications are accepted. The application window is open from 16 June 2026 to 06 July 2026, and registration is complete only once the application fee is successfully paid through the online payment gateway. Candidates can access the application form directly at www.bankofbaroda.bank.in/Career.htm, under the Career section's "Current Opportunities" page on www.bankofbaroda.bank.in.

  • Direct Link to apply Bank of Baroda Professionals Recruitment 2026

Key Roles and Responsibilities

A few common themes run across most of these positions. The Vice President and Deputy Vice President-level Relationship Head and Senior Relationship Manager roles centre on growing and managing the bank's existing corporate relationships in their specialised segment - real estate, MNCs, credit-lite clients, or conglomerates - sourcing new-to-bank corporate clients, cross-selling fee-based products such as forex and cash management services, and building account plans with opportunity-income analysis while keeping risk exposure within the bank's Exposure Risk Framework. The Transaction Banking roles (Head-Product Sales, Senior Product Sales Manager, and Product Sales Manager) focus on selling trade, forex, and cash management products, managing transaction banking client relationships, and driving fee income and CASA balances. The AVP-level Conglomerate/Real Estate and Credit Lite roles concentrate on credit appraisal, risk evaluation, and timely account monitoring, while the DVP-Head Market Intelligence Unit role is centred on gathering and summarising market and industry intelligence to provide competitive insights to management. Across all positions, the bank has reserved the right to modify or add to these responsibilities at any time.

Application Fee

Bank of Baroda has set a two-tier, non-refundable application fee for this recruitment. Unreserved (UR), EWS, and OBC candidates must pay Rs 850 (inclusive of GST), plus applicable payment gateway charges, while SC, ST, PWD, Ex-servicemen/DESM, and Women candidates pay Rs 175 (inclusive of GST), plus payment gateway charges. The fee can be paid online using a Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, or UPI. It is payable irrespective of whether an online test is eventually conducted and irrespective of whether the candidate is shortlisted for an interview, and once paid, it will not be refunded under any circumstances.

In-Hand Salary Calculator 2026

Contract Tenure, Remuneration and Credit Score Requirement

These are fixed-term contractual roles, and the tenure depends on the grade. For AVP I and AVP II, the initial contract runs for 5 years from the date of joining and can be renewed at the bank's discretion, subject to satisfactory performance, for one additional period of up to 5 years. For VP and DVP, the initial contract is for 3 years and can be extended in increments of 1 year each, provided the total engagement does not exceed 5 years. In every case, the engagement automatically ends at contract expiry unless renewed, and it cannot continue beyond the candidate reaching 60 years of age.

Remuneration is not fixed in the notification - the bank states it will be decided based on the selected candidate's qualifications, experience, overall suitability, last drawn salary, and the prevailing market benchmark for the position, and the place of posting will depend on the bank's requirement at any of its offices or branches in India.

A distinctive eligibility condition for this recruitment is credit history: candidates must have a CIBIL score of 680 or above at the time of joining, and the bank has explicitly stated that candidates who have defaulted on loan or credit card repayments, or against whom adverse reports exist with CIBIL or other credit-rating agencies, will be deemed ineligible for appointment - a check the bank can apply at any stage, including after joining.

Selection Process

Selection proceeds through Application Scrutiny, followed by an Online Test, Psychometric Test, or any other test the bank considers suitable, and then a Personal Interview along with compensation negotiation for those selected. The Psychometric Test and/or Interview assess a candidate's personality, communication, clarity, problem-solving ability, efficiency, and willingness to work anywhere in the country. To qualify in the Personal Interview, a candidate must score at least 60% for the Unreserved category and 55% for Reserved category candidates, though the bank reserves the right to revise this cut-off. If multiple candidates tie at the cut-off mark, they are ranked in descending order of age, meaning the older candidate ranks higher.

Call letters will be sent only to the email ID registered in the online application - no hard copies will be sent by post or courier - so candidates must keep that email account active and check it regularly. At the interview, candidates must carry a valid photo ID such as a PAN card, passport, driving licence, voter's card, or Aadhaar card with photograph; a Ration Card will not be accepted as identity proof for this recruitment, and candidates who have legally changed their name must produce the original Gazette notification or affidavit reflecting the new name.

How to Apply: Step-by-Step Guide

  1. Visit the Bank of Baroda website www.bankofbaroda.bank.in (or directly www.bankofbaroda.bank.in/Career.htm) and go to the Career section's "Current Opportunities" page.
  2. Register using a valid personal email ID and contact number that you can keep active throughout the recruitment process, since all call letters and updates will be sent there.
  3. Fill in the online application form carefully - no field can be edited once you click Submit - and ensure your name is spelt exactly as it appears on your certificates and mark sheets.
  4. Upload your bio-data, scanned photograph (200×230 pixels, 20-50 KB), and signature (140×60 pixels, 10-20 KB) in JPG/JPEG format, along with PDF copies of your eligibility documents.
  5. Pay the applicable application fee online using a Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, or UPI through the integrated payment gateway.
  6. After successful payment, download and print the system-generated e-receipt and application form for your records; if a transaction fails, register again and make the payment afresh rather than assuming the first attempt succeeded.
  7. Complete the process well before 06 July 2026, since the bank has advised against waiting until the last date to avoid login failures caused by heavy website traffic.

Documents Required (Upload and Interview)

Two separate sets of documents matter here - what must be uploaded with the online application, and what must be physically produced at the interview.

Troubleshooting and Common Mistakes to Avoid

Keep your scanned photograph between 20-50 KB and your signature between 10-20 KB, both in JPG/JPEG format - files outside this range, or in the wrong format, will trigger an error and block submission. Sign only in your normal handwriting and never in capital letters, since the bank has specified that signatures in capital letters will not be accepted, and any mismatch between your call-letter signature and your interview-day signature can lead to disqualification.

If an online payment fails or you are unsure whether it went through, do not assume it succeeded - register again and complete the payment, since the fee is non-refundable. Use an updated browser and a stable internet connection while filling the form, and avoid waiting until the last day or last few hours before 06 July 2026, since heavy website traffic close to the deadline is a common cause of failed submissions. Always download and save your acknowledgement number, e-receipt, and printed application form immediately after payment, as these are needed for future reference and at the interview. Finally, double-check every field - especially your name, category, and date of birth - before clicking Submit, since no corrections are allowed after the online application has been submitted.

📄 Complete Details & Notification

Bank of Baroda is hiring for 86 vacancies across 5 officer-level posts in its Corporate and Institutional Credit (C&IC) department, ranging from Manager to Chief Manager grade in both Credit Analyst and C&IC Relationship roles. Online registration opened on 16 June 2026, and the last date to apply and pay the fee is 6 July 2026. Eligible candidates need a postgraduate finance qualification or CA/CMA/CS/CFA, relevant banking credit experience, and willingness to serve anywhere in India.

Add FJA on  As Preferred Source

Bank of Baroda C&IC Recruitment 2026: Key Dates You Need to Know

This recruitment drive was announced under advertisement number BOB/HRM/REC/ADVT/2026/10. There are only two dates that matter for candidates: when the application window opens and when it closes, since the bank has not yet announced an online test date.

Event Date
Online Registration Starts 16 June 2026
Last Date for Application Submission & Fee Payment 6 July 2026

Registration is treated as complete only once the application fee is paid online on or before 6 July 2026; the date of the online test, if conducted, will be announced separately to candidates through their registered email and the bank's website.

86 Vacancies Across 5 Posts: Full Position-wise Breakdown

The 86 vacancies are divided into two job families: Credit Analyst posts and C&IC Relationship posts, each spanning three or two seniority grades respectively. Vacancy count, age limit, and required post-qualification experience vary by grade, so candidates should check the exact post they qualify for before applying.

Credit Analyst Posts (Manager, Senior Manager & Chief Manager)

Credit Analyst posts focus on appraising corporate credit proposals and carry the highest vacancy count in this recruitment, with the Senior Manager grade alone accounting for 38 of the 86 total seats.

C&IC Relationship Posts (Senior Manager & Chief Manager)

C&IC Relationship posts are client-facing roles centred on sourcing and managing corporate borrowers rather than appraising proposals, and together they account for 43 of the 86 vacancies.

Across all 5 posts, work experience of less than 6 months in any organisation as on 1 June 2026 will not count toward eligibility unless it forms part of a candidate's current employment, and time spent in a clerical cadre role is not counted at all.

Eligibility Criteria: Qualification, Age & Work Experience

The educational qualification for Bank of Baroda C&IC Recruitment 2026 is identical across all 5 posts, while the age limit and experience requirement increase with seniority. Candidates should also note that the bank will only consider qualifications from institutions recognised by the Government of India or bodies like the AICTE.

  • Educational Qualification: Graduation in any discipline, plus a Post Graduate Degree or Diploma with specialisation in Finance (or its equivalent), OR a professional qualification such as CA, CMA, CS, or CFA.
  • Age: Calculated as on 1 June 2026, ranging from a minimum of 25 years (Manager grade) to a maximum of 42 years (Chief Manager grade).
  • Nationality: Indian citizens are eligible, along with certain categories of Nepali, Bhutanese, Tibetan refugee, and Indian-origin candidates from specified countries, subject to an eligibility certificate from the Government of India where applicable.
  • Posting Condition: Only candidates willing to serve anywhere in India should apply, since the bank can post selected officers to any branch or office at its discretion.

Reservation & Category-wise Vacancy Distribution

Reservation in Bank of Baroda C&IC Recruitment 2026 is applied separately for each of the 5 posts rather than as one combined pool, and candidates cannot change their declared category after registering online. Out of 86 total vacancies, 69 carry some form of category-based roster point while 17 remain unreserved.

CIBIL Score Requirement: A Credit History Check Unique to This Recruitment

Unlike most government recruitment notifications, this advertisement makes personal credit history a formal eligibility condition. Candidates need a minimum CIBIL score of 680 at the time of joining the bank, since this post involves handling corporate credit decisions.

Anyone who has defaulted on loan repayments or credit card dues, or who has adverse reports from CIBIL or other external credit assessment agencies, will be treated as ineligible for appointment. The bank has reserved the right to reject a candidate's selection at any stage, including after joining, if their credit profile turns out to be unsatisfactory.

Probation Period and Mandatory Service Bond

Selected candidates do not join in a permanent capacity immediately; they first complete a probation period, and they must also commit to a minimum service period backed by a financial bond.

  • Probation Period: 12 months (1 year) of active service from the date of joining.
  • Service Bond: Candidates must serve the bank for a minimum of 3 years from the date of joining, or pay ₹5 lakh in lieu of completing the bond period.

The exact bond terms will be confirmed in each selected candidate's offer letter and are subject to revision as per the bank's prevailing policy.

Application Fee for Bank of Baroda C&IC Recruitment 2026

The application fee for this recruitment is fixed by category and must be paid online; it is non-refundable even if the online test is not conducted or the candidate is not shortlisted for an interview.

SC, ST, PWD, ESM/DESM & Women ₹175 (inclusive of GST) + Payment Gateway Charges

Selection Process: Online Test, Psychometric Assessment & Interview

Selection for Bank of Baroda C&IC Recruitment 2026 can include application scrutiny, an online test, a psychometric assessment, a group discussion, and a personal interview, though the bank retains the right to skip or modify any stage. Final selection depends on combined performance across whichever stages are actually conducted.

Online Test Pattern (Tentative)

If a written test is held, it will be a 150-mark, 150-minute online exam split into four sections, three of which only need to be passed rather than scored well in.

Section Test Questions Marks Duration
1 Reasoning 25 25 75 minutes (combined)
2 English Language 25 25
3 Quantitative Aptitude 25 25
4 Professional Knowledge 75 150 75 minutes
Total 150 225 150 minutes

Reasoning, Quantitative Aptitude, and Professional Knowledge will be available bilingually in English and Hindi, while the English Language section will be in English only. Sections 1 to 3 are qualifying only and do not count toward the final score; candidates need at least 40% in General/EWS or 35% in Reserved categories to clear each of these sections, and there is no negative marking anywhere in the test.

Personal Interview & Final Merit

Candidates who clear the online test (or are otherwise shortlisted) move on to a psychometric assessment and/or personal interview, where the minimum qualifying score is 60% for General category and 55% for Reserved category candidates. If two or more candidates tie at the cut-off mark, the older candidate is ranked higher in the merit list.

The online test, if conducted, is tentatively planned across more than two dozen cities, including Mumbai, Delhi/NCR, Bangalore, Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Pune, Ahmedabad-Gandhinagar, Jaipur, Lucknow, Baroda, Bhopal, Chandigarh-Mohali, and several other regional centres, with the final allotted centre confirmed in the call letter.

Documents Required During the Recruitment Process

Candidates do not need to upload every certificate while registering online, but they must be ready to produce the following documents in original, along with self-attested photocopies, at the interview stage or whenever the bank asks for them.

  • Printout of the interview call letter and the system-generated online application form
  • Proof of Date of Birth (Birth Certificate, SSLC/Std. X marksheet, or equivalent)
  • A valid photo identity proof such as PAN Card, Passport, Driving Licence, Voter's Card, or Aadhaar card (Ration Card is not accepted)
  • Year-wise/semester-wise mark sheets and the final degree/diploma certificate
  • Caste certificate for SC/ST/OBC candidates, with the OBC certificate carrying a valid non-creamy-layer clause
  • Disability certificate from the District Medical Board, for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities
  • Income and Asset Certificate, for candidates applying under the EWS category
  • Service/discharge book, pension payment order, and rank proof, for ex-servicemen candidates
  • No Objection Certificate from the current employer, for candidates already working in government, quasi-government, or public sector roles
  • Documentary proof of declared work experience, such as appointment letters, salary slips, or relieving letters

Step-by-Step Guide: How to Apply Online

Bank of Baroda accepts applications for this recruitment only through its official website; no offline or postal applications will be considered.

  1. Visit www.bankofbaroda.bank.in and navigate to the Careers section, then Current Opportunities.
  2. Register using a valid personal email ID and contact number that you can keep active until the recruitment process is complete.
  3. Fill in personal, educational, and work experience details carefully, since no changes are allowed once the form is submitted.
  4. Upload your photograph (200 x 230 pixels, 20-50 KB) and signature (140 x 60 pixels, 10-20 KB) in JPG/JPEG format, signed in your normal handwriting and not in capital letters.
  5. Upload your resume, Date of Birth proof, educational certificates (combined in one PDF), and category/PWD/experience certificates where applicable, each as a PDF on A4 size not exceeding 500 KB.
  6. Pay the applicable application fee online using a Debit Card, Credit Card, Net Banking, or UPI.
  7. Save and print the system-generated application form and fee receipt for your future reference.

Apply Online for Bank of Baroda C&IC Recruitment 2026

Job Profile: What Will You Actually Do in This Role?

The two job families under this recruitment involve noticeably different day-to-day work, which is worth understanding before choosing which post to apply for.

Credit Analyst roles (Manager/Senior Manager/Chief Manager) are appraisal-focused: examining new and existing corporate credit proposals, conducting credit due-diligence on financial, industry, and business risk, coordinating with Relationship Managers, and ensuring compliance in corporate accounts.

C&IC Relationship roles (Senior Manager/Chief Manager) are client-facing: maintaining relationships with existing corporate clients, sourcing new-to-bank corporate borrowers, cross-selling ancillary business, and creating account plans with opportunity income analysis for corporate borrowers.

Mistakes That Could Cost You This Opportunity

Several avoidable errors can disqualify an otherwise eligible candidate from Bank of Baroda C&IC Recruitment 2026, so it helps to check these before hitting submit.

  • Assuming any postgraduate degree qualifies - only a finance-specialised PG degree/diploma or a CA/CMA/CS/CFA qualification meets the educational criteria.
  • Not checking your CIBIL score in advance - a score below 680, or any default history, can lead to rejection even after selection.
  • Counting clerical-cadre banking experience toward the eligibility criteria, which is explicitly excluded.
  • Including work experience of less than 6 months from a previous organisation, which will not be counted unless it is part of your current employment.
  • Submitting more than one application - only the latest valid one is retained, and fees paid for earlier ones are forfeited.
  • Selecting a category casually, since no change of category is allowed after registration and an invalid OBC/EWS claim without supporting certificates can affect your candidature.
  • Overlooking the 3-year/₹5 lakh service bond commitment before deciding whether to accept the role if selected.
  • Waiting until the last date to register, risking last-minute website load issues for which the bank takes no responsibility.

Stipend and Leave - MSC Bank Cooperative Intern 2026

The monthly remuneration for selected Cooperative Interns is a consolidated ₹25,000 per month, paid by the respective State Cooperative Bank or District Central Cooperative Bank where the intern is posted. This is not a regular salary but a fixed internship stipend for the one-year duration. T.A.D.A. (Travelling and Daily Allowance) will also be provided by the respective posting bank.

Component Details
Monthly Stipend ₹25,000 (Consolidated)
Internship Duration 1 Year

Other Leave Leave without remuneration
Holidays As applicable to the respective posting bank
T.A.D.A. Provided by the respective bank

Roles and Responsibilities of Cooperative Intern

Candidates applying for the MSC Bank Cooperative Intern Programme 2026 will be assigned substantive responsibilities at the grassroots level. The intern is not merely an observer - they are expected to coordinate with Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) and other primary cooperatives, and prepare weekly progress reports for the Ministry of Cooperation. This is a full-time programme, and interns must observe the working hours of the concerned bank.

Key duties include:

  • Coordinating with Primary Agricultural Credit Society (PACS) and other primary cooperatives to provide guidance for implementing Ministry of Cooperation initiatives
  • Solving day-to-day problems faced by PACS in computerisation, preparation of business plans, projects, financing issues, and various approvals
  • Preparing and sharing weekly status reports on the implementation of Ministry of Cooperation initiatives, in coordination with the State Cooperative Bank and District Central Cooperative Banks

Selection Process - MSC Bank Cooperative Intern Recruitment 2026

The selection process for the MSC Bank Cooperative Intern Recruitment 2026 is straightforward - applications are accepted offline, and only shortlisted candidates will be called for an interview. Final selection is at the discretionary power of the Bank/Selection Committee. There is no written examination mentioned in the notification.

Step 1 - Application Screening: The bank shortlists candidates from the offline applications received based on eligibility criteria.

Step 2 - Interview: Only shortlisted candidates are called for a personal interview. The exact date and venue of the interview are communicated to shortlisted candidates directly.

Step 3 - Final Selection: The Selection Committee's decision on final selection is discretionary and binding.

How to Apply Offline - MSC Bank Cooperative Intern Apply 2026

The MSC Bank Cooperative Intern Apply 2026 process is entirely offline - there is no online application portal for this recruitment. Candidates must download the prescribed application form (Annexure-I) from the bank's website, fill it in their own handwriting, attach all supporting documents, and physically submit it to the bank's Mumbai head office before the deadline. Applications submitted after 5:15 PM on 10 July 2026 will not be accepted.

Step-by-step application process:

  1. Visit the official MSC Bank website at https://msc.bank.in/career and download the Application Form (Annexure-I)
  2. Fill the application form in your own handwriting with all required details including name, address, date of birth, educational qualifications, MBA/PGDM specialisation, computer proficiency, work experience, and references
  3. Affix a recent passport-size photograph in the designated space and sign in the signature box
  4. Attach self-attested photocopies of all relevant qualification certificates, computer proficiency certificate, and experience certificates (if any)
  5. Provide details of two references - bankers, professionals, or government officials who are residents of India, holders of responsible positions, and not related to you
  6. Place the completed application and all documents in a sealed envelope
  7. Write "Application for the post of Cooperative Intern" on the envelope
  8. Submit or send the sealed envelope to:
    The Joint Manager (OSD), HRD&M Department, The Maharashtra State Cooperative Bank Ltd., Sir Vithaldas Thackersey Memorial Building, 9, Maharashtra Chamber of Commerce Lane, Fort, Mumbai – 400001
  9. Ensure delivery on or before 10 July 2026 till 5:15 PM

Documents Required - MSC Bank Cooperative Intern 2026

Candidates must enclose self-attested photocopies of all supporting documents along with the application form (Annexure-I). Submitting incorrect or false information makes the candidate liable for disqualification and, if appointed, for dismissal from service without notice.

Required documents to enclose with the application:

  • Passport-size photograph (affixed on the form)
  • Proof of date of birth
  • Marksheets and certificates from Matriculation through MBA/PGDM (including Bachelor's degree)
  • MBA/PGDM degree or provisional certificate confirming successful completion
  • Computer proficiency certificate (MS-CIT or equivalent)
  • Any additional professional qualification certificates (JAIIB/CAIIB, certifications, etc.)
  • Work experience certificates, if applicable
  • Details of two references (bankers/professionals/government officials, non-relatives)
  • PAN Card copy
  • Aadhaar Card copy

Important Terms and Conditions for MSC Bank Cooperative Interns

Candidates must clearly understand that the MSC Bank Cooperative Internship 2026 is not a job offer and does not create any right or claim for regular employment with MSC Bank or any associated institution. The internship can be discontinued at any time without payment of financial benefit if the intern's performance is unsatisfactory or if the intern is absent without authorisation. Interns are also bound by strict confidentiality obligations regarding bank documents, policies, and business plans.

Key terms to note:

  • This is a full-time internship programme - interns must observe bank working hours
  • The internship may be terminated at any time without assigning reasons
  • Interns must not interact with media (print/electronic/social media) or represent the bank without express permission
  • Interns must maintain confidentiality of all documents, reports, and information received during the internship - violation entails legal consequences
  • No intern can post work-related content on social media without written permission from competent authority
  • The internship confers no right to employment with the bank or associated institutions

Troubleshooting and Common Mistakes to Avoid

Since the MSC Bank Cooperative Intern application process is entirely offline, several common errors can lead to rejection. Being aware of these before submitting your application saves time and avoids disappointment.

  • Applying while still pursuing MBA/PGDM: The notification is clear - candidates currently pursuing the 2-year MBA/PGDM are not eligible. Only those who have already completed the degree should apply.
  • Missing the 5:15 PM deadline on 10 July 2026: This is not a midnight deadline - it is 5:15 PM sharp. Applications received even minutes after 5:15 PM on 10 July will not be accepted. Plan for early submission or courier delivery with tracking.
  • Not filling the form in own handwriting: The application form (Annexure-I) must be handwritten by the candidate. Typed or printed personal details in the form may be grounds for rejection.
  • Not mentioning MBA/PGDM specialisation clearly: The form has a checkbox for specialisation (Marketing Management, Cooperative Management, Agri Business Management, Rural Development Management). Leaving this blank creates ambiguity.
  • Omitting computer proficiency certificate: Computer proficiency is listed as an essential qualification. Candidates who do not enclose proof of MS-CIT or equivalent certification risk rejection.
  • Providing relatives as references: The notification explicitly states that references must not be relations. Providing a family member as a reference is a disqualifying error.
  • Wrong envelope superscription: The envelope must be labelled "Application for the post of Cooperative Intern." Using any other labelling or no labelling may result in the envelope being misrouted.
  • Submitting only the form without supporting documents: Self-attested photocopies of all qualification certificates must accompany the form. An incomplete application without supporting documents will not be processed.

Unlike most government job notifications, this Bank of Baroda recruitment includes a specific financial credibility check. This is an important and somewhat unique eligibility condition candidates must be aware of.

Candidates must maintain a satisfactory credit history, and a minimum CIBIL score of 680 or above is required at the time of joining. Candidates who have defaulted on loan repayment or credit card dues, or against whom adverse reports exist from CIBIL or other external credit rating agencies, will be deemed ineligible for appointment. Remuneration and Location of Posting
